en: Now, the Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa: In this world, indeed, both gods and humans existed. Those gods, when departing for the heavenly world, said to Agni: The Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa, 1.1.1–2: In this world, indeed, both gods and humans existed.
Those gods, when departing for the heavenly world, said to Agni:
"Be you the overseer of this world for us.
To them, Agni said: (The Establishment of the Sacred Fires). KB_1.1.4: Agni spoke to them.
KB_1.1.5: Now, as for that which I am—the most terrible to touch—KB_1.1.6: humans are those who do not show reverence [to it].
(The Establishment of the Sacred Fires)
KB_1.1.7: "How will that be yours among men?
KB_1.1.8: Those gods said:
KB_1.1.9: "We shall indeed deposit those terrible bodies of yours [among men]."
(Agnyādhāna) KB 1.1.10: "Now, that body of yours which is auspicious, effective, and worthy of sacrifice—KB 1.1.11: with that you shall exist here among men."
(On the establishment of the sacred fires): For him, they placed the *pavamāna* fire in the waters;
the *pāvaka* fire in the wind.
KB_1.1.14: [He places it] in the sun, the pure one.
(The Installation of the Fires) KB_1.1.15:
Now, that very body of his which was auspicious, effective, and worthy of sacrifice—
KB_1.1.16: By means of that [fire], he heated [the world] here for the sake of human beings.
(The Establishment of the Sacred Fires) KB_1.1.17: These indeed are the bodies of Agni.
KB_1.1.18: Therefore, when one sacrifices to these deities;
KB_1.1.19: therein Agni becomes pleased, together with his limbs and his bodies.
(The Establishment of the Fires)
KB_1.1.20: These indeed become three.
KB_1.1.21: For these worlds are three. KB_1.1.22: Thus, he attains these very worlds.
(On the Establishment of the Sacred Fires) KB_1.2.1: The ritual procedure for the Full Moon sacrifice belongs to the first [night]. KB_1.2.2: That of the New Moon sacrifice belongs to the second.
KB_1.2.3: By means of that, the New and Full Moon sacrifices become undertaken by him.
(The Establishment of the Fires) KB_1.2.4: The two *saṃyājyā* verses for the first [offering] are those containing the word *īḍita* and the word *havyavāṭ*.
KB_1.2.5: That is the form of the *saṃyājyā* verses. KB_1.2.6: [This applies] to the second [offering] for the two Agnis.
(The Establishment of the Fires)
KB_1.2.7: For he sacrifices to two fires.
KB_1.2.8: The third [offering] consists of seven *sāmidhenī* verses. KB_1.2.9: Or rather, the *iṣṭi*s and animal sacrifices consist of seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses.
(On the establishment of the sacred fires: KB_1.2.10: Thereby he obtains the *iṣṭi* and the *paśubandha* sacrifices.
KB_1.2.11: The two portions of clarified butter (*ājyabhāga*) are accompanied by the word "sat" (*sadvantau*).
KB_1.2.12: "May I be," thus one establishes the sacred fires (*agnyādhāna*). KB_1.2.13: "May I exist," thus he desires.
KB_1.2.14: Even if he, though being like one who lacks heroic sons, establishes the sacred fires;
KB_1.2.15: he quickly comes into being [with sons].
(The Establishment of the Sacred Fires)
KB_1.2.16: He quickly attains the state of being one whose merit is to be enjoyed.
KB_1.2.17: He who performs [the sacrifice] with two [verses] that possess the word *sat*.
KB_1.2.18: The two *saṃyājyā* verses are *virāj*s.
KB_1.2.19: Śrī is the Virāj; she is food and the eating of food. (The laying of the fires) KB_1.2.20: For the attainment of Śrī, the Virāj, and the eating of food.
KB_1.2.21: These indeed are in the *gāyatrī* metre.
KB_1.2.22: For Agni is of the *gāyatrī* nature, and his metre is the *gāyatrī*.
(The Establishment of the Sacred Fires)
KB_1.2.23: He establishes the fires with that very same *chandas*.
KB_1.2.24: These [formulas] are indeed performed in a low voice (*upāṃśu*).
KB_1.2.25: For the establishment of the fires is indeed the emission of seed.
(On the establishment of the sacred fires) KB_1.2.26:
Semen is indeed poured out silently.
KB_1.2.27: They become suitable.
KB_1.2.28: Whatever is appropriate in the sacrifice is successful; it is for the very success of the sacrifice.
(The Establishment of the Fires) KB_1.2.29: One should give twelve [cows].
KB_1.2.30: Twelve indeed are the months of a year. KB_1.2.31: [This is] for the attainment of the year itself.
(The Establishment of the Fires)
KB_1.2.32: He gives a horse as the thirteenth [item].
KB_1.2.33: This is for the attainment of that which is the thirteenth month.
(The Establishment of the Sacred Fires)
KB_1.3.1: The gods and the asuras were engaged in conflict over these worlds.
KB_1.3.2: From among them, Agni departed.
KB_1.3.3: He entered the seasons.
KB_1.3.4: Those gods, having slain the Asuras and conquered them, sought after Agni. KB_1.3.5: Yama and Varuṇa beheld him.
They invited him; they informed him;
they granted him a boon.
(On the Establishment of the Sacred Fires) KB_1.3.9: He chose this boon:
KB_1.3.10: "May the fore-offerings and the after-offerings be mine exclusively; may clarified butter be mine from the waters, and the human being from the plants."
(On the Establishment of the Sacred Fires) KB_1.3.11: Therefore they say, "The *prayāja*s and *anuyāja*s belong to Agni; the clarified butter belongs to Agni.
KB_1.3.12: By means of that, the gods indeed prevailed.
(Regarding the establishment of the sacred fires:
The Asuras are defeated;
he prospers through his own self.
KB_1.3.15: He who knows this has an enemy who is far away.
KB_1.3.16: Regarding this they ask, "In which season should one re-establish the fires? (The Re-establishment of the Fires).
KB_1.3.17: "In the rainy season," so some say.
KB_1.3.18: For in the rainy season all desires are indeed present.
KB_1.3.19: It is for the attainment of all desires whatsoever.
(On the re-establishment of the sacred fires): In the middle of the rainy season, having observed the *punarvasu* lunar mansion, he should re-establish the fires with the mantra:
"May wealth, which finds its way back, come to me again."
(Regarding the establishment of the sacred fires:
Furthermore, it is for the attainment of one's further desires.
Indeed, at that time during the first half of the month, it does not coincide again with the two Vasus.
(On the establishment of the sacred fires):
KB_1.3.24: That new moon which occurs after the full moon of Āṣāḍha;
KB_1.3.25: on that [new moon], one should establish the fires again.
KB_1.3.26: That [fire] again becomes united with the Vasus.
(The Establishment of the Sacred Fires) KB_1.3.27: On the new moon day, the desired object is attained.
KB_1.3.28: [The fire] has arrived during the rainy season. KB_1.3.29: [The fire] has arrived again during the two months of Punarvasu. (The Establishment of the Sacred Fires)
KB_1.3.30: Therefore, one should establish the sacred fires again in that [situation].
KB_1.3.31: There is a sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa) on five potsherds.
KB_1.3.32: The Paṅkti meter consists of five feet.
KB_1.3.33: The sacrifice is indeed fivefold; [this is] for the attainment of the sacrifice itself.
(The Establishment of the Fires) KB_1.4.1:
He performs the fore-sacrifices and after-sacrifices with the case-endings.
The fore-sacrifices and after-sacrifices are indeed the seasons. By means of them, they bring him together with the seasons.
(The Establishment of the Sacred Fires)

KB_1.4.4: “Come forward for the feast,” “We choose Agni as the messenger,” “By Agni is Agni kindled,” “May Agni strike down the Vṛtras,” “We meditate upon the praise of Agni,” and “The mortal who [serves] with devotion toward Agni”—these are the opening words of the verses; these are the case-endings (*vibhaktayaḥ*) [for the fire-installation].
KB_1.4.5: These indeed become six.
There are six seasons. By means of the seasons, he thus brings him back together again. (The Establishment of the Sacred Fires)
KB_1.4.8: He performs the first and last *prayāja* and *anuyāja* offerings in their proper order.
KB_1.4.9: In this way, his [sacrifice] does not suffer any deficiency regarding the *prayāja*s and *anuyāja*s.
KB_1.4.10: The first *ājyabhāga* offering belongs to Vṛtrahan, for the very purpose of slaying evil.
(On the Establishment of the Sacred Fires) KB_1.4.11: Moreover, his fire remains unkindled from the ritual procedure (*tantra*) of the Full Moon sacrifice.
KB_1.4.12: "One should first perform [the rite] for Agni the Awakened with the verse *agnim stomena bodhaya*," so say some.
(On the re-establishment of the sacred fires): "The fire of him who lets his fire go out is, as it were, asleep;
this [re-establishment] awakens it again."
(Regarding the *agnyādhāna*):
However, the *vārtraghna* [offering] remains as it was.
"O Agni, you purify the lives" (*agna āyūṃṣi pavase*) is the invitatory verse (*puronuvākyā*) for the subsequent [offering].
"Flow on"— this is the form belonging to Soma;
for the sacrificial rite belongs exclusively to Agni.
KB_1.4.19: In that he recites the verses of the Pavamāna [Stotra], KB_1.4.20:
thus his portion of the clarified butter belonging to Soma becomes unexhausted.
(The Establishment of the Sacred Fires)
KB_1.5.1: The *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses consist of *paṅkti* meters.
KB_1.5.2: A *paṅkti* consists of five feet. KB_1.5.3: The sacrifice is indeed fivefold; [this is] for the attainment of the sacrifice itself.
(The Establishment of the Fires) KB_1.5.4: They are interwoven.
KB_1.5.5: For these vital breaths, being as it were interwoven, enjoy the self.
KB_1.5.6: That entire [offering], including the *sāmidhenī* verses, is performed in a low voice (*upāṃśu*) up until the first two *anuyāja* offerings.
(Agnnyādhāna) KB_1.5.7:
For it is from this point that the case-endings (*vibhakti*) become connected in sequence.
KB_1.5.8: Moreover, all desires indeed reside in the case-endings. KB_1.5.9: Therefore, they are performed in a whisper.
(The Establishment of the Fires)
KB_1.5.10: For the attainment of all desires indeed. KB_1.5.11: But he performs the final after-offering (*anuyāja*) loudly. KB_1.5.12: He recites the *sūktavāka* and the *śaṃyuvāka* loudly.
(On the Establishment of the Sacred Fires) KB_1.5.13:
"Just as one who knows [the way] would call out what was hidden so that it becomes manifest," KB_1.5.14:
"in this same way, he makes his desires manifest by saying, 'I have attained them.'"
(Regarding the establishment of the fires:
Regarding this triad, some perform it in a whisper—the two *vibhakti* formulas, the subsequent *ājyabhāga*, and the oblation.
(The Establishment of the Fires)
KB_1.5.16: "For this much indeed arises from what is adventitious.
KB_1.5.17: That [syllable] is pronounced in a low voice (*upāṃśu*) and is unexpressed (*nirukta*).
KB_1.5.18: In the beginning, form is indeed twofold: expressed and unexpressed.
(On the Establishment of the Sacred Fires) KB_1.5.19: By that very act, he thereby obtains it. KB_1.5.20: Some, indeed, perform everything as pertaining to Agni.
KB_1.5.21: One should not do it in that manner.
KB_1.5.22: For this [rite], the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) is either a worn-out garment that has been mended, or a refurbished chariot, or a draft-ox, or gold.
(The Establishment of the Sacred Fires)
KB_1.5.23: For this is indeed a repeated rite.
KB_1.5.24: The Ādityas are the second [offering].
KB_1.5.25: Aditi is indeed the foundation.
KB_1.5.26: It is for the sake of stability, indeed, for the sake of stability.
(The Establishment of the Fires) KB_2.1.1: This Gharma, namely the Agnihotra, is indeed being offered forth.
KB_2.1.2: That indeed is the *gharma* which shines yonder.
KB_2.1.3: It is this very one that he gratifies. (The Agnihotra) KB_2.1.4: He offers it both in the evening and in the morning.
KB_2.1.5: [One offers] to Agni in the evening and to Sūrya in the morning.
KB_2.1.6: For the day belongs to Sūrya and the night to Agni. (Agnihotra) KB_2.1.7:
Thus, at the very outset, he gratifies both day and night.
KB_2.1.8: One should offer with milk.
KB_2.1.9: Milk, indeed, is the essence of all plants.
(Agnihotra) KB_2.1.10: Thus, by means of all essences, one gratifies the fires.
Regarding this, they say: "One should offer only of food. For all this [world] is the food of Agni; thus, by means of his own food, he gratifies the fires. (The Agnihotra)
KB_2.1.14: Having placed [the oblation] upon the *gārhapatya* fire, one should offer it into the *āhavanīya*.
(Agnihotra) KB_2.1.15: The *gārhapatya* is indeed for cooking. KB_2.1.16: The *āhavanīya* is for offering.

KB_2.1.17: Therefore, having placed [the oblation] over the Gārhapatya fire, he should offer it in the Āhavanīya fire. (Agnihotra) KB_2.1.18: He makes the embers two-pointed. KB_2.1.19: By this, he extends these two worlds.

KB_2.1.20: Therefore, these two worlds, though existing together, are as if separate. (The Agnihotra) KB_2.1.21: Now, when he heats [the milk] after placing it on the fire and then shines it forth, KB_2.1.22: he is indeed cooking it thereby.
KB_2.1.23: Now, as for why he pours water back [into the fire]: KB_2.1.24: Water, indeed, constitutes all sacrificial oblations (*havis*) in their entirety.
KB_2.1.25: It is for the sake of the completeness of the oblation. (Agnihotra)
KB_2.1.26: Now, as for why he cuts off [the portion] again;
KB_2.1.29: For the threefold is the work of the gods;
KB_2.1.30: He carries it away as if without cutting it off. (The Agnihotra)
KB_2.1.31: Thus, the sacrificer becomes one who is not liable to fall away.
KB_2.1.32: Then, with the *upaveṣa* (fire-stirring stick), he touches the embers from the south, saying, "Homage to the gods. KB_2.1.33:
For the gods do not disregard an act of homage.
KB_2.1.34: He should push back the embers that have been well-shaken out.
KB_2.1.35: Thus, indeed, nothing belonging to him perishes, not even that which moves within his home.
(The Agnihotra) KB_2.2.1: He should draw up [the milk] four times.
KB_2.2.2: Or all this is fourfold.
KB_2.2.3: For the attainment of all this very thing.
KB_2.2.4: He should draw up [the milk] five times (at the Agnihotra).
KB_2.2.5: The sacrifice is indeed fivefold; [this is] for the attainment of the sacrifice itself. KB_2.2.6: The *upasads* are to be understood as part of the *agnihotra*.
KB_2.2.7: Having drawn out [the milk], he places it down to the north of the *gārhapatya* fire. (The *agnihotra*)
KB_2.2.8: By that, he attains this world.
KB_2.2.9: When about to offer in the Āhavanīya fire, he offers a second [oblation]. KB_2.2.13: He places a fuel-stick of Palāśa wood upon the fire. (Agnihotra)
The palāśa tree is indeed Soma;
this is the first oblation of Soma.
It is one span in length. (Agnihotra)
KB_2.2.17: For these vital breaths of the self are indeed the size of a span.
KB_2.2.18: Having moved the fuel-sticks two finger-breadths beyond [the fire], he offers the oblation as if whispering. (Agnihotra) KB_2.2.19:
For food is placed in the mouth at a distance of two finger-breadths.

KB_2.2.20: One who desires a village should offer [the oblation] when the fire is smoking. (Agnihotra) KB_2.2.21: One who desires Vedic splendor should offer it when the fire is blazing. KB_2.2.22: One who desires cattle should offer it upon the embers.
KB_2.2.23: "Having added [fuel]," thus indeed it is established. (The Agnihotra) KB_2.2.24: For here indeed all these desires are obtained.
KB_2.2.25: Having offered both oblations, he mutters [the following].
KB_2.2.26: "May that blessing which belongs to a successful sacrifice be fulfilled for me. (Agnihotra) KB_2.2.27:
Indeed, whatever blessing belongs to a successful sacrifice, that accrues to the sacrificer.
KB_2.2.28: [He offers] the two subsequent descending oblations (*uttarāv avatī āhutī*).
One should offer the oblation. (Regarding the *agnihotra*:
By means of ever higher [offerings], one attains the heavenly worlds.
One touches the embers with the base of the *sruk* ladle.
KB_2.2.31: He places the sacrificer in heaven itself in that world. (Agnihotra) KB_2.3.1: He lifts the ladle twice toward the north. KB_2.3.2:
Having thus gratified Rudra in his own quarter, he dismisses him. (Agnihotra)

KB_2.3.3: Therefore, one should not stand to the north of that which is being offered. KB_2.3.4: [One should think: "May I not be left behind in the service of this entire god. (The Agnihotra) KB_2.3.5: He wipes it toward the west at night from the north.
KB_2.3.6: He thus causes the sun to set.
KB_2.3.7: In the morning, he holds [the ladle] upright toward the south.
(Agnihotra) KB_2.3.8: He thus causes the sun to rise.
KB_2.3.9: That which he wipes off first, he smears onto the *kūrca* grass mat.
KB_2.3.10: By this, he gratifies the plants. (Agnihotra) KB_2.3.11: That which is the second [portion], he places it with his right hand, palm upwards, upon the *kūrca*.
KB_2.3.12: By that [act], he gratifies the ancestors. (Agnihotra) KB_2.3.13:
Now, when he eats [the remainder] with the forefinger, KB_2.3.14:
he gratifies the embryos by means of the former [act].
KB_2.3.15: Therefore, embryos move about without eating. (Agnihotra) KB_2.3.16: Birds [move] to the north. KB_2.3.17:
Therefore, birds eat almost anything at all, and they urinate as if it were white. (Agnihotra)
KB_2.3.18: Now, as for the fact that he consumes [the remnant] with the *sruva* ladle; KB_2.3.19:
thereby he gratifies both what has been and what is to be. (The Agnihotra) KB_2.3.20:
Now, as for the fact that he licks the *sruva* ladle clean.
KB_2.3.21: By that, he gratifies all the divine beings. KB_2.3.22:
Now, when he cleanses the offering-spoon (*sruc*), KB_2.3.23:
by that, he gratifies the demonic divine beings. (The Agnihotra)
KB_2.3.24: Now, when he pours out water toward the east and the north, he thereby gratifies the Gandharvas and Apsarases. KB_2.3.25–26:
Then, when he lifts up the offering-ladle toward the east and the north—(in the Agnihotra)—
KB_2.3.27: Thus he places Rudra himself in his own quarter.
KB_2.3.28: In this way, by means of the Agnihotra, he gratifies all beings. (Agnihotra) KB_2.4.1: "One should offer only in the Āhavanīya fire," so say some.
KB_2.4.2: However, one should offer oblations in all of them. KB_2.4.3: For these are established for the purpose of offering oblations. KB_2.4.4: Four [oblations] are offered in the Gārhapatya fire.
KB_2.4.5: Four [logs] are placed on the *anvāhāryapacana* fire; KB_2.4.6: two on the *āhavanīya* fire. (Agnihotra) KB_2.4.7:
These amount to ten.

KB_2.4.8: The *daśadaśinī* is the *virāj*. KB_2.4.9: The *virāj* is prosperity (*śrī*), the eating of food. KB_2.4.10: [This is] for the attainment of prosperity, the *virāj*, and the eating of food. (The Agnihotra)
KB_2.4.11: He who thus offers the Agnihotra as perfected by the Virāj [metre] attains all desires. KB_2.4.12: Having offered, he then stands in attendance upon the fires. (Agnihotra)

KB_2.4.14: Having thus gratified the gods, he finally speaks for his own purpose. KB_2.4.15: And as to why he touches the calf— KB_2.4.16: Therefore it is called the *vātsapra* (the "calf-touching" [hymn]). (Agnihotra)
KB_2.4.17: Thus, the cattle do not tend to stray away from the sacrificer.
KB_2.4.18: Now, when he sips water and releases the vow, KB_2.4.19: he thereby places the vow within the waters. (Agnihotra)
KB_2.4.20: His vow-observance is protected until the next oblation.

KB_2.4.21: Furthermore, when he is about to depart on a journey or when he has already gone abroad, he pays homage to the fires. (Agnihotra) KB_2.4.22: Indeed, that which is a loud cough is a salutation to the deity.
KB_2.4.23: Moreover, he thus entrusts himself to the fires. (Agnihotra) KB_2.4.24:
And also to those who follow after him. KB_2.4.25:
Now, as for the fact that he deposits the fires into the two kindling woods: (Agnihotra)
KB_2.4.26: The two kindling woods (*araṇī*) are indeed the chariot of the gods.
KB_2.4.27: By means of them, he thus causes those [fires] to mount upon the chariot of the gods.
KB_2.4.28: By means of this chariot of the gods, he attains the heavenly world in safety. (Agnihotra)
KB_2.4.29: Furthermore, in that he churns [the fire] again and again, by that very act his re-establishment of the sacred fires (*punarādheya*) is attained. (Agnihotra) KB_2.4.30:
Whatever joys there are in food, in drink, and in sexual union; KB_2.4.31: [these are attained].
KB_2.4.32: These [offerings] are performed by you continuously and without interruption throughout the night.
KB_2.4.33: For them, the night is the *kārotara* vessel.
KB_2.4.34: And whatever joys there may be—(the Agnihotra).
KB_2.5.1: All these are born from food alone.
KB_2.5.2: Those gods said:
KB_2.5.3: "How indeed shall we receive these joys for one such as ourselves? (The Agnihotra).
They drew out the essence from the waters upward;
those became the plants and the trees. They drew out the essence from the plants and the trees upward.
That became its fruit. (The Agnihotra) drew out the essence from above the fruit;
that became food.
KB_2.5.10: From food, he drew forth its essence upward. KB_2.5.11: That became semen. (The Agnihotra) KB_2.5.12: From semen, he drew forth its essence upward.
KB_2.5.13: He became that person.
KB_2.5.14: This very person, when he breathes in or breathes out—(the Agnihotra)—KB_2.5.15:
That is not done by means of the out-breath or the in-breath, for one does not say, "I have breathed out," or "I have breathed in."

KB_2.5.16: By speech alone he says that [at the Agnihotra]. KB_2.5.17: Having merged speech into breath and out-breath, they become composed of speech. KB_2.5.18: Now, as for what one sees with the eye [at the Agnihotra]...
KB_2.5.19: One does not say of that [object] with the eye, "I saw it. KB_2.5.20:
One speaks of it by means of speech alone. KB_2.5.21: That eye merges into speech; it becomes composed of speech. (The Agnihotra)
KB_2.5.22: Now, that which one hears with the ear— KB_2.5.23: one does not say by means of the ear, "I heard this";
KB_2.5.24: rather, one says it by means of speech alone. (The Agnihotra)
KB_2.5.25: That ear merges into speech; it becomes composed of speech.
KB_2.5.26: Now, that which one intends with the mind— KB_2.5.27: One does not say that [intention] with the mind, saying, "I have formed this intention. (The Agnihotra)
KB_2.5.28: By speech alone he says that. KB_2.5.29: Then the mind enters speech; it becomes composed of speech.
KB_2.5.30: Now, whatever one touches with the limbs—whether it be well-formed or ill-formed—in the Agnihotra.
KB_2.5.31: "He does not say with his limbs, 'I have touched this well-behaved one' or 'this ill-behaved one';
KB_2.5.32: "He says it by speech alone. (Agnihotra) KB_2.5.33: "Thereupon, the whole self enters into speech; he becomes composed of speech."
This very point has been declared by a Ṛgvedic verse:
"No abode whatsoever is purified apart from Indra.
Now, Indra is indeed speech.
KB_2.5.37: For indeed, without speech, no domain whatsoever is purified.
(Agnihotra) KB_2.6.1: He offers in the evening with the formula: "Agni is light, light is Agni. KB_2.6.2: Although it is already light, he says "light."
KB_2.6.3: He speaks the truth. (Agnihotra) KB_2.6.4: His self consisting of speech becomes composed of truth. KB_2.6.5: The gods, indeed, consist of truth.
KB_2.6.6: Then he offers with the words, "Svāhā! (Agnihotra). KB_2.6.7: The gods accept this offering of his, which has been offered as truth.
KB_2.6.8: Indeed, at the head of the night, he speaks the truth. (Agnihotra)
KB_2.6.9: Even if he should speak falsely after that time, KB_2.6.10: what he has spoken indeed becomes true for him. (The Agnihotra) KB_2.6.11: For he speaks the truth at the head of the night.
KB_2.6.12: Then, in the morning, he offers the oblation with the mantra: "Sūrya is light, light is Sūrya. KB_2.6.13: Though it is already light, he says, "Light. KB_2.6.14: He speaks the truth.
KB_2.6.15: His self consisting of speech becomes one consisting of truth. (Agnihotra) KB_2.6.16: The gods, indeed, consist of truth.
KB_2.6.17: Then he offers with the utterance "svāhā."
The gods accept this oblation of his when he has offered it with truth. (Agnihotra) At the head of the day, he speaks the truth;
even if he should speak falsely thereafter, [the gods still accept it].
KB_2.6.21: Indeed, his speech becomes truly uttered. (The Agnihotra) KB_2.6.22: For during the day, one speaks the truth at the head [of the day].
KB_2.6.23: This very fire, rising as the sun, offers itself as an oblation.
KB_2.6.24: At sunset, yonder sun, whose self is the fire, offers itself into the fire.

(The Agnihotra) KB_2.7.1: Night indeed offers itself into day; day and night [offer themselves into one another]. KB_2.7.2: Exhalation indeed offers itself into inhalation; inhalation [offers itself] into exhalation.
KB_2.7.3: Indeed, these six offer one another as their own selves. (The Agnihotra) KB_2.7.4: He who knows these six as being offered— KB_2.7.5:
even though he does not offer them, his Agnihotra becomes truly offered.

KB_2.7.6: For one who offers in this very manner, his oblation becomes offered twice even while he is actually sacrificing. KB_2.7.7: Even if one who knows thus offers the Agnihotra with only a little, KB_2.7.8: these gods indeed accept his two oblations.

KB_2.7.9: Moreover, he whom even the gods eat but once—(the Agnihotra)—KB_2.7.10: from that very act he becomes immortal. KB_2.7.11: Indeed, one who knows this becomes composed of truth and composed of immortality—(the Agnihotra).
KB_2.7.12: Just as, indeed, for one who possesses faith, speaks the truth, and practices austerity, [the oblation] becomes offered;
KB_2.7.13: even so, indeed, does his [Agnihotra] become offered.
KB_2.7.14: He who, knowing thus, performs the Agnihotra; KB_2.7.15: therefore, one who knows thus should perform the Agnihotra.
KB_2.7.16: They deliberate whether it should be offered after sunrise or before sunrise. (Agnihotra)
KB_2.8.1: He who offers when [the sun] has risen, KB_2.8.2: he thereby performs hospitality for the great god, the Impeller (Prasavitṛ). KB_2.8.3:
Now, as for him who offers before sunrise—
KB_2.8.4: This is indeed the guest-offering he makes to the great deity who is already present. (Agnihotra) KB_2.8.5: Therefore, the offering should be made before sunrise.
KB_2.8.6: Regarding this, Vṛṣaśuṣma Vātāvata, one of the ancestors, being old and lying down at night, saw both oblations being offered and said:

KB_2.8.7: "They offer both oblations only at night," [it is said regarding the Agnihotra]. KB_2.8.8: "For it is by means of the night," he said. KB_2.8.9: "We shall be speakers. (We shall be speakers.)
"Right now we have gone to that world for the sake of the ancestors. (Agnihotra) KB_2.8.10:
"Moreover, they will not have faith in him. KB_2.8.11:
"But because on both days the Agnihotra was offered... (Agnihotra)
KB_2.8.12: Or rather, it is offered on the following day; at this very time it is offered. KB_2.8.13: "Only at night"—this is what the maiden possessed by the Gandharva said.
(Agnihotra) KB_2.8.14: "They offer both oblations only at night."

KB_2.8.15: "For it is at night," she said. KB_2.8.16: One should offer the oblation at the junction [of day and night]. (Agnihotra) KB_2.8.17: Indeed, this ocean that carries everything away is day and night.
KB_2.8.18: These two junctions (*saṃdhye*) are indeed its two fords (*tīrtha*) that provide a firm footing.
KB_2.8.19: Just as one might cross the ocean by means of two fords that provide a firm footing, such is this [crossing].
KB_2.8.20: That he offers the oblation at the junction [is like that crossing]. (Agnihotra)
KB_2.8.21: Moreover, day and night are indeed the divine army of the traveler that intends to slay him. (Agnihotra) KB_2.8.22: The two twilights are its two wings.
(Agnihotra) KB_2.8.23: Just as one might quickly traverse a journey by means of two wings, such is that [the Agnihotra]. (Agnihotra)
KB_2.8.24: That he offers at the junction [of day and night];
KB_2.8.25: Now, these two—the day and the night—are indeed the two arms of Virāj, which are death itself.
KB_2.8.26: It is just as if one were to escape by slipping through the space between the two arms of Virāj while intending to seize her; such is that [offering].
Regarding the *agnihotra* offering at the juncture [of day and night],
Kauṣītaki used to say this:
"In the evening, when the sun has set but before darkness falls— at that time one should offer."
KB_2.9.3: It has the path of the gods as its banner. (Agnihotra) KB_2.9.4: By undertaking that very [path], one goes safely to the heavenly world.
KB_2.9.5: One should offer the oblation at that time in the morning, before sunrise, when the darkness has been dispelled. (Agnihotra)
KB_2.9.6: Its banner is the path of the gods.

Śyāma and Śabala were indeed the two who dug up his Agnihotra. Day, indeed, is Śabala;
Night is Śyāma. (The Agnihotra)

Now, he who offers it during the day—

KB_2.9.15: Śabala indeed stirs up his Agnihotra. (Agnihotra) KB_2.9.16: Therefore, one should indeed offer at whatever time it may be. KB_2.9.17: One should meditate upon the success of the offering; one should meditate upon the success of the offering. (Agnihotra)
KB_3.1.1: That which he observes as the fast for the New and Full Moon sacrifices;

KB_3.1.4: "May the gods eat my oblation. KB_3.1.5: "One should observe the fast on the earlier full moon," says Paiṅgya. KB_3.1.6: "On the later," says Kauṣītaki. (DpM)
KB_3.1.7: That which rises after sunset is the established rule. KB_3.1.8: One should fast on the preceding full moon, provided that the moon is not yet perceived before the new moon. KB_3.1.9:
By fasting, one gratifies the former [deity].
KB_3.1.10: By that which he sacrifices, he [reaches] the northern [region].
KB_3.1.11: He should fast on the northern day.
KB_3.1.12: Indeed, the ocean swells toward the north following Soma as its deity.

KB_3.1.13: This indeed is the truth regarding the gods, namely the moon; therefore, one should observe the fast on the later [lunar day]. KB_3.1.14: Therefore, one should observe the fast on the later [lunar day]. (DpM) KB_3.2.1: Now, as for that which he mutters before the *sāmidhenī* verses:
KB_3.2.2: He thereby performs a rite for well-being.

KB_3.2.5: By means of the thunderbolt itself, he thus strikes away the evil of the sacrificer. KB_3.2.6: He utters "him" three times. KB_3.2.7: For the thunderbolt is indeed threefold.
KB_3.2.8: He thereby transforms it into the thunderbolt itself.
KB_3.2.9: By means of this threefold thunderbolt, the gods indeed drove the Asuras out from these worlds.
KB_3.2.10: In the same way, the sacrificer now drives his hateful rivals out from these worlds by means of this very threefold thunderbolt.
KB_3.2.11: He recites eleven *sāmidhenī* verses.
KB_3.2.12: The *triṣṭubh* meter indeed consists of eleven syllables.
KB_3.2.13: Indra is connected with the *triṣṭubh*.
KB_3.2.14: Through that, one attains both Indra and Agni.
(DpM) KB_3.2.15: By reciting the first verse three times and the last verse three times, it amounts to fifteen.
(DpM) KB_3.2.16: Indeed, there are fifteen days in the bright fortnight and the dark fortnight. (DpM)
KB_3.2.17: By means of those *sāmidhenī* verses, one attains the first and the second fortnights.
KB_3.2.18: Furthermore, the *sāmidhenīs* are indeed a thunderbolt (*vajra*). KB_3.2.19: For the thunderbolt is fifteenfold.
KB_3.2.20: By means of the thunderbolt itself, he thus strikes away the evil of the sacrificer. KB_3.2.21:
And as to why he recites the first verse three times and the last verse three times— KB_3.2.22:
He thereby ties the two side-beams of the sacrifice for stability and so that it does not fall apart.
KB_3.2.23: Indeed, there are three hundred and sixty syllables of these [verses].
(DpM) KB_3.2.24: There are indeed three hundred and sixty days in a year. KB_3.2.25: Thus, by means of the *sāmidhenī* verses, one attains the days of the year. (DpM)
KB_3.2.26: These [verses] are indeed in the *gāyatrī* meter.
KB_3.2.27: For Agni is of the *gāyatrī* nature, and his meter is the *gāyatrī*.
KB_3.2.28: Thus, he praises Agni by means of his own very meter.
KB_3.2.29: They become appropriate.
KB_3.2.30: That which is appropriate in the sacrifice is successful; it is for the very success of the sacrifice.
KB_3.2.31: At the third utterance of the *uttamā*, he joins the *nigada* with the *praṇava*.
"O Agni, you are great, O Brāhmaṇa, descendant of Bharata.
For Agni is indeed the descendant of Bharata;
he indeed bears the oblation to the gods.

KB_3.3.4: Now, as for why he recites the ancestral lineage (*ārṣeya*) of the sacrificer: KB_3.3.5: For the gods do not eat the oblation of one who has no ancestral lineage. KB_3.3.6: Therefore, he recites his ancestral lineage.
KB_3.3.9: Now he appends this fifteen-word *nigada* formula. (DpM) KB_3.3.8: This indeed is the *nivid* of the *sāmidhenī* verses. KB_3.3.9: Therefore, it consists of fifteen words.

KB_3.3.10: For there are fifteen *sāmidhenī* verses. KB_3.3.11: That [offering] indeed becomes one not fashioned out of meters (*acchandas-kṛta*). KB_3.3.12: Indeed, all this is twofold: that which is fashioned out of meters and that which is not fashioned out of meters.
KB_3.3.13: "With all of that, I shall praise Agni. KB_3.3.14: Having combined its seven steps, he should pause.

KB_3.3.16: For the attainment of all the meters. KB_3.3.17: Now four, then four.
KB_3.3.18: For this whole world consists of groups of four.
KB_3.3.19: This is for the attainment of this entire [sacrifice]. KB_3.3.20: Now, as to why he invokes the deities individually: KB_3.3.21: For separate oblations have been taken for them.
KB_3.3.22: Therefore, he invokes the deities by separating them [one by one]. KB_3.3.23: Now, as for the fact that he invokes Agni with Agni— KB_3.3.24:
This indeed is the sacrificial body of Agni, which is his carrier of oblations.
KB_3.3.25: That which is yonder, shining above this world like a light in the sky, is indeed that [light].
KB_3.3.26: When he says, "O Agni, bring Agni hither," KB_3.3.27: he thereby means, "Bring her hither."

KB_3.3.28: Now, when he invokes the gods who drink the clarified butter, (DpM) KB_3.3.29: he thereby invokes the fore-offerings and the after-offerings. KB_3.3.30: Then, when he invokes Agni for the office of the Hotṛ, [he thereby invokes the sacrificial fee].
KB_3.3.31: He invokes the Sviṣṭakṛt [deity] therein. KB_3.3.32:
Now, when he invokes his own greatness, KB_3.3.33:
he thereby invokes Vāyu.
KB_3.3.34: Or rather, wind is the inherent greatness of fire.
(DpM) KB_3.4.1: For by means of that, having attained [it], one goes to greatness. KB_3.4.2: Moreover, what he recites with speech, he sacrifices with speech.
KB_3.4.3: By that, indeed, his own greatness becomes sacrificed.

KB_3.4.4: He says, "And bring them hither, O Jātavedas, and sacrifice with those well-yoked ones. KB_3.4.5: "And bring the gods hither, O Jātavedas, and sacrifice to the deities with those well-yoked ones"—this is what he thereby says to him.
KB_3.4.6: Now, as for that which he mutters after the *sāmidhenī* verses;
KB_3.4.7: the *sāmidhenīs* are indeed a thunderbolt;
KB_3.4.8: he thus appeases that very [thunderbolt] both in front and behind.
KB_3.4.9: Now, when he causes the two offering-ladles (*srucau*) to be taken up by means of the formula for taking up the ladles;
KB_3.4.10: he thereby yokes the divine chariot (*deva-ratha*) in order to present the oblation (*havis*) to the gods;
KB_3.4.11: by means of that divine chariot, he attains the heavenly world (*svarga-loka*) in safety.
KB_3.4.12: He performs the fore-offerings.
KB_3.4.13: The seasons, indeed, are the fore-offerings. KB_3.4.14: Thus he gratifies the seasons. (DpM)
KB_3.4.15: These indeed become five.
KB_3.4.16: By means of them, whatever is fivefold—whether pertaining to the deities or pertaining to the self—one attains it all.
KB_3.4.17: He offers the *samidh* oblations; he thereby worships the spring itself.
KB_3.4.18: Or rather, in the spring all this is kindled.
KB_3.4.19: He sacrifices to Tanūnapāt; [he thereby worships] Gīṣpati himself. KB_3.4.20: For in summer one heats the body.
KB_3.4.21: He offers the *iḍā* oblation; [this is] indeed the rainy season.
KB_3.4.22: For it is through the rains that the food fit for eating arises when it has been praised. KB_3.4.23: He offers the *barhis* oblation; [this is] indeed the autumn.
KB_3.4.24: For in autumn, the plants are most abundant.
KB_3.4.25: He performs the sacrifice ending with the *svāhā*-utterance; thus he reaches the winter. KB_3.4.26: Indeed, in winter, all this is consecrated with *svāhā*.
KB_3.4.27: Regarding this they say: "Since there are five fore-offerings (*prayāja*) and six seasons, at which season does he sacrifice for this sixth season?
KB_3.4.28: When he pours [the butter] together during the fourth fore-offering, he thereby distributes it among the others. KB_3.5.1:
Now, when he brings together the deities during the final fore-offering...
KB_3.5.2: He thereby makes these [deities] partakers of the *prayāja* offerings.
KB_3.5.3: Just as Agni becomes a sharer in all the oblations, KB_3.5.4: so does he make the deities sharers in that portion of Agni.
KB_3.5.5: "In this case, he does not say 'Agni from the Hotṛ'. KB_3.5.6:
"The fore-sacrifices (*prayāja*) are indeed cattle.
KB_3.5.7: "Sviṣṭakṛt is Rudra."
KB_3.5.8: "Lest I cause the cattle of the sacrificer to perish through Rudra.
KB_3.5.9: "Svāhā! May the gods who drink the clarified butter, O Agni, graciously partake of the clarified butter"—thus some say. KB_3.5.10: One should not do so.
KB_3.5.11: Indeed, half of the sacrifice is the clarified butter (*ājya*), and half is the oblation (*havis*). KB_3.5.12: If one were to mention only one of these two, KB_3.5.13:
then half of the sacrifice would be completed, and half would remain uncompleted.
KB_3.5.14: Therefore, one should simply say: "Svāhā! May the gods who drink the clarified butter, being pleased, O Agni, partake of the oblation of clarified butter.
KB_3.5.15: Now, as for the fact that on the full moon day there are two *ājyabhāga* offerings [with verses] slaying Vṛtra;
KB_3.5.16: For by means of the Full Moon sacrifice, Indra indeed slew Vṛtra.
KB_3.5.17: Now, as for the two [verses] containing the word *vṛdh* on the new moon day;
KB_3.5.18: for here the moon undergoes waning;
KB_3.5.19: it is this [offering] that causes it to swell and makes it grow. (DpM)
KB_3.6.1: Those two indeed have the *juṣāṇa* as their *yājyā* verses. KB_3.6.2: For they possess the same oblation as the *prayāja*s. KB_3.6.3:
Moreover, the *juṣāṇa* is indeed the Brahman.
KB_3.6.4: Only the Brāhmaṇas thus present the oblation to the gods.
KB_3.6.5: These two indeed consist of threefold [stomas].
KB_3.6.6: [They are] the *ye yajāmahe* formula, the *nigada*, and the *vaṣaṭ*-call.
KB_3.6.7: The two *ājyabhāga* offerings are indeed the eye.
KB_3.6.8: For the eye is threefold—white, black, and red. KB_3.6.9: One does not perform those two at the animal sacrifice nor at the Soma sacrifice. (DpM)
KB_3.6.10: "The sacrifice is indeed sightful by means of the animal. KB_3.6.11: "I shall not perform a four-eyed, loathsome sacrifice. KB_3.6.12:
"Now, as for [the verse] beginning with *yadāvatyoṇ*..."

Having thus called upon [the gods], he then presents the oblation to the deities.
KB_3.6.15: These [verses] are indeed in the *gāyatrī* and *triṣṭubh* meters.
KB_3.6.16: The *gāyatrī* is indeed the *brahman*.
KB_3.6.19: The *triṣṭubh* is the *kṣatra*. (DpM)
KB_3.6.20: By means of the Brahman and the Kṣatra alone, he thus presents the oblation to the gods.
KB_3.6.21: He utters the *vaṣaṭ* at the end of the *ṛc*.
KB_3.6.22: In this way, all his *yājyā* verses become possessed of their proper form.
KB_3.6.23: He utters "vaṣaṭ" six times.

KB_3.7.3: That which is long is the *bṛhat*.
KB_3.7.4: Now, this [earth] is indeed the Rathantara, and yonder [heaven] is the Bṛhat.

Therefore, he sacrifices to him at the end.
For that [sacrifice], the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses consist of those two meters, while the *nigada* is distinct.
