KB_3.9.22: Now, when they bring the *anvāhārya* rice, KB_3.9.23: this indeed constitutes the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) for the New and Full Moon sacrifices.

KB_3.9.24: Therefore they bring it [the fuel] for him. KB_3.9.25: Now, as for the fact that he consecrates the fuel-stick with a mantra: KB_3.9.26: This is indeed the one remaining stick of the faggot.
Therefore, he praises this [goddess]. Now, as for why he performs three after-offerings (*anuyāja*):
these worlds are indeed three.
KB_3.10.3: By this, he indeed attains these very worlds. KB_3.10.4: Now, as for the fact that he pronounces everything as "the highest" (uttama);
KB_3.10.5: The *sviṣṭakṛt* offering is indeed a firm foundation; it is for the sake of stability.

KB_3.10.6: Now, as for the fact that he recites the *sūktavāka*: (DpM) KB_3.10.7: The *sūktavāka* is indeed a firm foundation; it is for the sake of stability. KB_3.10.8: Now, as for the fact that he mentions Heaven and Earth: (DpM)
Heaven and earth are indeed the two supports; [it serves] for support alone.
"Agni has enjoyed this oblation," so some say.
One should not do so.
KB_3.10.12: The deity turns back toward him, thinking, "The sacrifice shall be performed again. KB_3.10.13: [She thinks], "He will offer the oblation to me again.
KB_3.10.14: She frustrates the sacrificer’s blessings when he says, "This is the oblation."

Therefore, one should simply say, "The oblation has been enjoyed; the oblation has been enjoyed. Moreover, those very deities whom he sacrifices to first, it is through them that he finds support in the end.
KB_3.10.18: Now, when he pronounces the name of the sacrificer in the *sūktavāka* [recitation], KB_3.10.19:
this indeed is the divine self of the sacrificer which the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) consecrate;
KB_3.10.20: therefore, he pronounces his name.
KB_3.10.21: For it is here that [the fire] is born.
(DpM) KB_3.10.22: One should take it up even if the teacher be present.
(DpM) KB_3.10.23: In this way, the sacrificer becomes one who is not displaced. (DpM)

KB_3.10.24: Now, they recite five blessings; three at the *iḍā* [offering], making eight in total. KB_3.10.25: By means of these, indeed, the gods attained all their desires (*aṣṭi*). KB_3.10.26: In the same way, the sacrificer likewise attains all his desires by means of these very [blessings].
KB_3.10.27: Then, having placed his joined palms upon the sacrificial grass (*barhis*) facing eastward, he mutters: "Homage, up... (DpM). KB_3.10.28:
For the gods do not go beyond a salutation.
KB_3.10.29: Now, as for the fact that he recites the *śamyorvāka* formula.
The *śamyor vāk* is indeed a firm foundation; [he recites it] for the sake of stability.
Furthermore, Śamyu Bārhaspatya indeed pacified all sacrifices;
therefore, he recites the *śamyor vāk*.
Now, as for why he touches water:
water is indeed peace and medicine;
thus, this very peace and medicine is performed in the sacrifice.
KB_3.11.1: Now, as for the fact that they perform the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings at the Gārhapatya fire;
KB_3.11.2: the wives indeed have a share in the Gārhapatya;
KB_3.11.3: the sacrificer has a share in the Āhavanīya.
Therefore, they perform the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings at the Gārhapatya fire.
(DpM) These indeed become four;
for a pair consists of four, and a pair is productive for the sake of procreation. (DpM)
KB_3.11.7: They indeed take place in a whisper.
KB_3.11.8: The Patnīsaṃyāja offerings are indeed the emission of semen.
KB_3.11.9: Semen is indeed emitted in a whisper. (DpM)
KB_3.11.10: They become suitable. KB_3.11.11:
Whatever is suitable in the sacrifice, that is successful; it is for the very success of the sacrifice.
(DpM) KB_3.11.12: Then [he offers to] Soma, Tvaṣṭṛ, the wives of the gods, and Agni Gṛhapati. (DpM)
Indeed, these deities rule over pairs.
They are gratified here;
being gratified, they bestow pairs upon him.
KB_3.12.1: He sacrifices first to Soma. KB_3.12.2: He thereby pours forth semen. KB_3.12.3: He sacrifices second to Tvaṣṭṛ.
Tvaṣṭṛ indeed transforms the emitted seed;
therefore, there are wives. For these are the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings.
Now, as for the fact that he sacrifices to Agni Gṛhapati at the end:
the wives are indeed the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering;
therefore, he sacrifices to him at the end.
KB_3.12.10: Now, as for him who touches water, its Brāhmaṇa explanation has been stated. KB_3.12.11:
Now, when he mutters a Ṛg-verse, he thereby effects a blessing. KB_3.12.12:
Now, as for his inviting Iḷā, his purifying himself, and his reciting the *śamyor-vāk* formula, their Brāhmaṇa explanation has been stated.
Now, as for the fact that he causes the wife to recite from the Veda:
the Veda is indeed the male,
and the wife is the female.
KB_3.12.16: He thus places the pair among the wives.
KB_3.12.17: Therefore, the wife places grass between her thighs. KB_3.12.18: Now, as for the fact that he spreads the Veda-grass.
By this, his New and Full Moon sacrifices become continuous.
Furthermore, by this very means, his Agnihotra becomes one for which the sacrificial grass has been strewn. Now, as for the fact that he worships while standing over the remnants of the Veda.
KB_3.12.22: He thus utters a blessing.
KB_3.12.23: Now, when he pays homage to the Āhavanīya fire, KB_3.12.24: having gratified the gods, he thereby utters his purpose at the very end.
Now, as for the fact that he touches water:
water is indeed peace and medicine. Thus, at the conclusion of the sacrifice, this very peace and medicine is performed; at the conclusion of the sacrifice, it is performed.

KB_4.1.1: By means of the *anunirvāpya* offerings, the gods indeed drove away the Asuras. KB_4.1.2: In the very same way, the sacrificer now drives away his hateful rivals by means of the *anunirvāpya* offerings.
(The *vikṛti* sacrifices)
KB_4.1.3: He offers a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra Vimṛdh.
KB_4.1.4: Indra, indeed, is the destroyer of adversaries. (The Vikṛti sacrifices)
He alone strikes down his adversaries. Furthermore, when he sacrifices to Indra on the full moon day, he thereby brings back the new moon sacrifice itself.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.1.7: In this case, if the sacrificer, having established the New and Full Moon sacrifices, should suffer a breakdown during the dark fortnight;
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.1.8: there shall be no displacement of his sacrifice.
KB_4.1.9: Now, as for the fact that one sacrifices to Aditi on the new moon day;
KB_4.1.10: it is for the sake of providing a support for the sacrifice.
KB_4.1.11: That [offering] becomes free from exhaustion because of the *saṃyājyā* verses.
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.2.1:
Now, therefore, [the ritual] for one who has slept during the day. KB_4.2.2:
Indeed, this person has strayed from the path of sacrifice.
KB_4.2.3: On whose fast-day the moon is seen in the east;
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.2.4: He offers a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Dātṛ.
Agni is indeed the giver;
he alone bestows the sacrifice upon him.
KB_4.2.7: For Indra the Bestower, [is offered] curd produced by evening milking.
KB_4.2.8: Indra, indeed, is the Bestower. (The Vikṛti sacrifices)
KB_4.2.9: He alone bestows the sacrifice upon him.
KB_4.2.10: [He offers] a caru-oblation of rice cooked in milk that has been milked in the morning to Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
Viṣṇu is indeed the sacrifice;
he himself bestows the sacrifice upon him when he approaches these deities.
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis):
"May I not go away from the path of sacrifice"—thus [he thinks].
Three bows constitute the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*).
KB_4.2.16: That is the form of the *svastyayana* [rite].
(The *vikṛti-iṣṭis*) KB_4.3.1:
Now, therefore, [the rite] for one who has been looked down upon (*abhyuddṛṣṭā*).
KB_4.3.2: "Come, indeed, he has strayed from the path of sacrifice.
KB_4.3.3: "He for whom the moon is seen in the west at the time of the Upavasatha [is one who has strayed].
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.3.4: He offers a cake on eight potsherds to Agni Pathikṛt.
KB_4.3.5: Agni, indeed, is the maker of paths.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
He alone causes him to fall upon the path of sacrifice.
[One offers] a cake on eleven potsherds to Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra;
for Indra is indeed the slayer of Vṛtra.
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.3.9:
He indeed causes him to fall back again onto the path of sacrifice.
KB_4.3.10: [There is] an offering to Vaiśvānara on twelve potsherds.
(Vikṛti Sacrifices) KB_4.3.11: That which shines yonder is indeed Vaiśvānara.
KB_4.3.12: He alone causes him to fall back again onto the path of sacrifice.
KB_4.3.13: Therefore, when he sacrifices to these deities, [it is because] KB_4.3.14:
[he thinks], "Lest I stray from the path of the sacrifice."
KB_4.3.15: A staff and sandals are the sacrificial fee.
KB_4.3.16: That is the form of fearlessness.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.4.1: Now, furthermore, regarding the Dākṣāyaṇa sacrifice.
KB_4.4.2: One desiring to perform the Dākṣāyaṇa sacrifice begins it on the full moon day of the month of Phālguna. (The Vikṛti sacrifices.)
KB_4.4.3: This full moon day of Phālguna is indeed the mouth of the year.
KB_4.4.4: Therefore, on that day, the *adīkṣitāyanas* (the preparatory rites for those not yet initiated) are performed.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.4.5: Now, Dakṣa Pārvati, having sacrificed with this sacrifice, obtained all his desires.
KB_4.4.6: Therefore, when one sacrifices with the Dākṣāyaṇa-yajña—(The Vikṛti offerings).

KB_4.4.7: For the attainment of all desires whatsoever; KB_4.4.8: one may obtain desire even in the case of destruction; KB_4.4.9: one should eat while meditating in the mind, thinking, "May I partake of King Soma, the Moon."
(Vikṛti Sacrifices) KB 4.4.10: Now, that King Soma is indeed the far-seeing moon. KB 4.4.11: The gods press him during the latter half of the month.
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.4.12:
Now, as for the fact that they observe the vows of the Dākṣāyaṇayajña during the latter fortnight; KB_4.4.13:
it is with the thought, "May I also partake in the drinking of Soma among the gods."

(Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.4.14: Now, as for the fact that on the day of preparation (*upavasatha*) one offers a sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) on eleven potsherds dedicated to Agni and Soma; KB_4.4.15: this is indeed that same Agni-Soma offering which belongs to the Soma sacrifice on the day of preparation.
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.4.16:
By that very [offering], he attains that same [result] for him. KB_4.4.17:
Now, as to why he performs the New Moon sacrifice in the morning.
KB_4.4.18: The day of the Soma-pressing belongs to Indra.
KB_4.4.19: By this, one attains that day of the Soma-pressing.
KB_4.4.20: Now, on the fast-day of the new moon, he offers a cake on twelve potsherds dedicated to Indra and Agni.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.4.21:
For the third pressing belongs to Indra and Agni by its very nature.
KB_4.4.22: By that, he obtains the third pressing.
(The modified sacrifices) KB_4.4.23:
Now, as for the curd offering dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa:
KB_4.4.24: Or the Anūbandhyā cow is dedicated to Mitra and Varuṇa.
KB_4.4.25: Thus one obtains the Anūbandhyā sacrifice.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.4.26: This very Soma has entered into the sacrifices as the oblation.
KB_4.4.27: Therefore, one who is not initiated observes the vow of the initiated.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.5.1: Now, therefore, [the ritual] of the Iḍādadh- sacrifice.
KB_4.5.2: One desiring to perform the Iḍādadh- sacrifice employs it at this very full moon; its Brāhmaṇa explanation has already been stated. (The Vikṛti sacrifices)
KB_4.5.3: This is the sacrifice for one who desires cattle and for one who desires food.
KB_4.5.4: One who desires cattle and one who desires food should sacrifice with it.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.5.5: Therein he performs the vows in that very same manner.
KB_4.5.6: For this is the summary of the Dākṣāyaṇayajña.
KB_4.5.7: Now, therefore, [follows] the Sārvaseniyajña.
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB 4.5.8: One intending to sacrifice with the Sārvaseni sacrifice performs it on this very full-moon day; its Brāhmaṇa has already been explained.
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.5.9: This, however, is the sacrifice for one who wishes to strike down [an enemy]. KB_4.5.10: He who should desire, "May I strike down my hateful rival," [should perform this sacrifice].
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.5.11: By this, he indeed strews the sacrificial ground. KB_4.5.12: Now, therefore, follows the Śaunaka sacrifice.
KB_4.5.13: One desiring to perform the Śaunaka sacrifice undertakes it on this very full moon day; the Brāhmaṇa explanation for that has already been stated.
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.5.14: This is the sacrifice for one desiring offspring. KB_4.5.15: One desiring offspring should sacrifice with it.
KB_4.5.16: That which the Adhvaryu prepares as the oblations is the form of procreation.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.6.1: Now, therefore, [concerning] the sacrifice of Vasiṣṭha.
KB_4.6.2: One desiring to sacrifice with the Vasiṣṭha-sacrifice begins on the new moon day of the month of Phālguna.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.6.3: The full moon is indeed Brahman.
The New Moon sacrifice is the ruling power (*kṣatra*).
This sacrifice is indeed like the ruling power. (The Modified Sacrifices)
KB_4.6.6: "With power, may I overcome my enemies.
KB_4.6.7: Vasiṣṭha, whose sons had been slain, desired: "May I prevail over the Saudāsas through offspring and cattle.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
He beheld this sacrificial rite, the Vasiṣṭha-sacrifice. Having sacrificed with it, he multiplied through offspring and cattle and surpassed the Saudāsas.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
In the same way, when the sacrificer, being a Vasiṣṭha, performs the sacrifice with this [offering],
he is propagated with offspring and cattle, and he overcomes his hateful rivals.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.6.12: Now, therefore, [the ritual] of the Sākamprasthāyya.
KB_4.6.13: One desiring to perform the Sākamprasthāyya offers it on this very new moon day; its Brāhmaṇa explanation has already been stated.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.6.14: This is the sacrifice for one who desires preeminence and for one who desires manly prowess.
KB_4.6.15: One who desires preeminence and one who desires manly prowess sacrifices with it.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.6.16: Therefore, when they establish themselves together;
KB_4.6.17: when they sacrifice together;
KB_4.6.18: when they consume together.
KB_4.6.19: Therefore, the Sākamprasthāyya [offering] is performed.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.7.1:
Now, therefore, concerning the Munyayana.
KB_4.7.2: Desiring to proceed by the path of the sages, he performs this very Full Moon sacrifice; its Brāhmaṇa explanation has already been stated.
(The Vikṛti sacrifices) KB_4.7.3: This is the sacrifice for one who desires all objects of desire.
KB_4.7.4: With that, one should sacrifice for the fulfillment of all desires.
KB_4.7.5: Now, therefore, [the description] of the Turāyaṇa [sacrifice].
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.7.6: One who desires to set out on the *turāyaṇa* sacrifice performs it at this very full moon; its *brāhmaṇa* explanation has been stated.
(The *vikṛti* sacrifices.
KB_4.7.7: This is the sacrifice for one who desires heaven.
KB_4.7.11: By means of the Brahman itself, he thus brings his self to fulfillment.
(The Vikṛti sacrifices) KB_4.7.12: There are indeed three oblations.
KB_4.7.13: There are indeed these three worlds.
KB_4.7.14: By this, he attains these very worlds.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.8.1: Now, therefore, [the ritual] of the Āgrayaṇa.
KB_4.8.2: One who desires food should sacrifice with the Āgrayaṇa when the rainy season has arrived and the śyāmāka grain is ripe. (The Subsidiary Sacrifices)
KB_4.8.3: He says, "Gather the *śyāmāka* grains.
KB_4.8.4: Whatever new moon day (*amāvāsyā*) may coincide with that time [is the one for the sacrifice].
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
Having sacrificed with that [offering], one should then sacrifice with this offering.
If it is the full moon day,
having sacrificed with this [offering], one should then sacrifice with the full moon sacrifice (*paurṇamāsa*).

(Vikṛti Sacrifices) KB_4.8.8: If, however, he should desire a lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*), KB_4.8.9: having observed a lunar mansion in the bright fortnight (*pūrvapakṣa*), he should sacrifice under whichever auspicious lunar mansion he may desire.

(Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.8.10: For this [sacrifice], there are seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses; the two *ājyabhāga* offerings have the word "sat" at their ends; the two *saṃyājyā* verses are *virāj*s; its *brāhmaṇa* explanation has been stated.
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.8.11: There is a caru-oblation for Soma.
KB_4.8.12: Soma is indeed the king of plants.
KB_4.8.13: Thus he gratifies him with his own domain.
(Vikṛti Sacrifices) KB_4.8.14:
Now, as for why he offers the honey-mixture (*madhuparka*); KB_4.8.15:
for this is the essence of wild animals.
(Vikṛti Sacrifices) KB_4.9.1: Now, when spring has arrived and the bamboo-grains have ripened;
KB_4.9.2: he says, "Uproot the bamboo-grains."

KB_4.9.3: Of this [sacrifice], this very [offering] is the section, this is the ritual framework (*tantra*), this is the deity, this is the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), and this is the Brāhmaṇa explanation. (The Modified Sacrifices) KB_4.9.4:
Some indeed perform that [offering] as dedicated to Agni, or to Varuṇa, or to Prajāpati; it has this very same ritual framework and this same Brāhmaṇa explanation.
(Vikṛti Sacrifices) KB_4.9.5:

Now, when the rice crop or the barley crop has arrived, he says, "Set aside the portions for the Āgrayaṇa sacrifice. KB_4.9.6: [He gives the command: "Set aside the portions for the Āgrayaṇa sacrifice."
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.9.7:
For this [sacrifice], this very [full moon] is the joint; this is the ritual framework. KB_4.9.8:
Now, as for the cake on twelve potsherds for Indra and Agni—
(Vikṛti Sacrifices) KB_4.9.9:
Indra and Agni are indeed the mouth of the gods. KB_4.9.10:
Thus, from the very beginning, he gratifies the gods.
(Vikṛti Sacrifices) KB_4.9.11: Now, as for the rice-pap offering to the Viśvedevas; KB_4.9.12: these Viśvedevas are indeed all the gods.
KB_4.9.13: For the gratification of all the gods.
(The Vikṛti sacrifices) KB_4.9.14: Now, as for the cake on one potsherd for Heaven and Earth.
KB_4.9.15: Heaven and Earth are indeed the accomplishers of the grain-crop.
(The Vikṛti sacrifices) KB_4.9.16: The earth is the foundation; he knows this through the food-offering.
KB_4.9.17: Therefore, when he sacrifices to these deities, [he thinks]: "Through these deities, I shall eat food that has been pacified.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.10.1: Now, he who gives the first cow [performs] this; KB_4.10.2:
for this is the first rite. KB_4.10.3:
If he should become weary of this.
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.10.4:
One should prepare the full-moon or new-moon oblation of new grain for the attainment of both.
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_4.10.5: Or rather, one should extend the oblations at either the full moon or the new moon sacrifice, so that there may be no omission of the deities.
(The *vikṛti* sacrifices) KB_4.10.6: Or rather, one should offer only barley-gruel as the morning and evening *agnihotra*, for the attainment of both [the old and the new grain].

(Vikṛti-iṣṭis) Or rather, having cooked a simple mess of boiled rice on the Gārhapatya fire, he should offer it on the Āhavanīya fire with portions of the new grain for these deities of the Āgrayaṇa sacrifice, making the Sviṣṭakṛt offering as the fourth, saying, "Svāhā to such-and-such a deity! Svāhā to such-and-such a deity!"—thus to ensure that no deity is omitted.
(Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
Alternatively, having caused the Agnihotra cow itself to eat the new grain, one should offer the evening and morning Agnihotra with her milk for the attainment of both.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis) These are the only offerings.
KB_4.10.10: Among these, one should sacrifice with whichever one he may desire.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis) KB_4.10.11:
But the three-oblation [sacrifice] remains fixed.
There are indeed these three worlds.
By this [rite], one attains these very worlds; by this, one attains these very worlds.
(The Vikṛti-iṣṭis)
KB_5.1.1: Now, therefore, [the ritual] of the Cāturmāsyas. KB_5.1.2: One who is about to perform the Cāturmāsyas begins them on the full moon day of Phālguna. KB_5.1.3:
For the full moon of Phālguna is indeed the mouth of the year.
The two Uttaraphalgunī stars are the head; the two Pūrvaphalgunī stars are the tail.
It is just as if the two ends of a moving object were to meet together.
In this very way, these two ends of the year meet together.
(The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice) When one performs the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice on the full moon day of Phālguna, one thereby gratifies the year at its very beginning. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice)
Moreover, these Cāturmāsya sacrifices are indeed medicinal sacrifices;
therefore, they are performed at the junctions of the seasons,
for it is at the junctions of the seasons that disease arises.
KB_5.1.13: These indeed become eight oblations. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.1.14: There are indeed eight oblations for four full-moon sacrifices.
KB_5.1.15: The Vaiśvadeva is the combination of four full-moon sacrifices. (The Cāturmāsya)
Now, when fire is churned—Prajāpati, indeed, is the Vaiśvadeva;
therefore, they produce this divine embryo. (The Cāturmāsya)

KB_5.1.19: Now, as for the fact that there are seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses, the two *ājyabhāga* offerings contain the word "sat," and the two *saṃyājyā* verses are *virāj*s—its *brāhmaṇa* explanation has already been stated. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice) KB_5.1.20: Now, as for the nine *prayāja*s, the nine *anuyāja*s, the eight oblations, and the whey (*vājina*) as the ninth;
KB_5.1.21: thereby one attains the *virāj* consisting of the lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*). (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice)

KB_5.2.1: Now, as for the fact that he sacrifices first to Agni and Soma among the deities; KB_5.2.2: these two are indeed the deities of the New and Full Moon sacrifices (Darśapūrṇamāsa). (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.2.3: Therefore, he sacrifices to these two first.
Now, as for the fact that he sacrifices to Savitṛ:
Savitṛ indeed is the lord of instigations;
[he sacrifices] so that there may be instigation by Savitṛ.
Now, as for the fact that he sacrifices to Sarasvatī:
Sarasvatī is indeed speech;
it is speech itself that he thus gratifies.
KB_5.2.10: Now, as for why he sacrifices to Pūṣan;
KB_5.2.11: Pūṣan is indeed that one who shines yonder; (Cāturmāsya) KB_5.2.12: it is him alone that he gratifies.
KB_5.2.13: Now, as for the fact that he sacrifices to the Maruts, the self-strong;
KB_5.2.14: the Maruts, the self-strong, are indeed terrible; KB_5.2.15: he thereby performs a healing rite.
Now, as for the curd offering (*payasyā*) dedicated to the Viśvedevas:
these Viśvedevas are indeed all the gods;
[this is] for the gratification of all the gods.
KB_5.2.19: Now, as for the cake on one potsherd for Heaven and Earth;
KB_5.2.20: Heaven and Earth are indeed the two foundations; it is for the sake of stability. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice) KB_5.2.21: Now, as for the fact that he gives a cow born first.
KB_5.2.22: For this is indeed the first ritual act. KB_5.2.23:

Now, as for the fact that he offers to the Vājins—whether before or after the *śamyu*-formula, or when the *vāka* has not been invoked—the Vājins are indeed divine horses. KB_5.2.24: The Vājins are indeed divine horses.
KB_5.2.25: By this, he indeed gratifies them. KB_5.2.26: Here, the gods together with the horses become gratified. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice) KB_5.2.27:
Furthermore, the Vājins are indeed the seasons.
KB_5.2.28: By this, he indeed gratifies the seasons.

KB_5.2.29: Now, as for the fact that he subsequently sacrifices with the Full Moon sacrifice; KB_5.2.30: thus, his Vaiśvadeva sacrifice has been performed during the waxing fortnight. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifices)
By means of the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice, Prajāpati indeed created offspring. Once created, they did not propagate; they ate the barley of Varuṇa.
Varuṇa then bound them with the nooses of Varuṇa. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifices)
KB_5.3.4: Those creatures, having approached their father Prajāpati, ran to him for refuge, saying:

"Learn that sacrificial rite (*yajña-kratu*) by which, having sacrificed, we may be completely released from the nooses of Varuṇa and from all evil. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.3.5: "Learn that sacrificial rite (*yajña-kratu*) by which, having sacrificed, we may be completely released from the nooses of Varuṇa and from all evil. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.3.6: Thereupon, Prajāpati perceived this sacrificial rite, the Varuṇapraghāsas.
He brought it; with it he sacrificed.
Having sacrificed with it, he gratified Varuṇa.
Varuṇa, being gratified, released the creatures from the bonds of Varuṇa and from all evil. (The Cāturmāsya sacrifices)
KB_5.3.10: Indeed, his offspring is completely released from the nooses of Varuṇa and from all evil, he who knows thus. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifices) KB_5.4.1:
Now, as for the fact that they lead forward the fire;
KB_5.4.2: It is that very same [fire] which they churn at the Vaiśvadeva sacrifice.
KB_5.4.3: They lead him forward in that very manner. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice) KB_5.4.4:
Now, regarding that which is churned, its Brāhmaṇa explanation has already been stated.

KB_5.4.5: Now, as for the fact that there are seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses, the two *ājyabhāga* offerings contain the word "sat," and the two *saṃyājyā* verses are *virāj*s—its Brāhmaṇa explanation has already been stated. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice)
KB_5.4.6: Now, as for the nine fore-offerings (*prayāja*s), the nine after-offerings (*anuyāja*s), and these nine oblations (*havis*);
by that, one attains the Virāj consisting of the lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*). (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.4.7–8:
There are five common recurring oblations (*saṃcara-havis*) belonging to the Vaiśvadeva [parvan], ending with the offering to Pūṣan. (The Cāturmāsya)

Regarding these, the Brāhmaṇa has been stated. Now, as for the cake on twelve potsherds for Indra and Agni: Indra and Agni are indeed the two supports; [it is offered] for the sake of support. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifices)
KB_5.5.1: Moreover, Indra is situated in the middle.
KB_5.5.2: Therefore, one sacrifices to him in the middle.
KB_5.5.3: Now, as for the curd-mixture dedicated to Varuṇa (in the Cāturmāsya).
Indra is indeed Varuṇa;
he is one whose food is milk.
Therefore, the *payasyā* belongs to Varuṇa. (The Cāturmāsya sacrifice)
Now, as for the curd offering (*payasyā*) dedicated to the Maruts:
the Maruts are indeed established in the waters;
therefore, one sacrifices to them with curd. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifices)
KB_5.5.10: For water is indeed milk.
KB_5.5.11: Moreover, the Maruts belong to Indra.
KB_5.5.12: Milk belongs to Indra.
KB_5.5.13: Therefore, there is the curd-offering (*payasyā*) for Marut. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.5.14:
Now, as for the cake on one potsherd (*ekakapāla*) for Ka; KB_5.5.15: Prajāpati, indeed, is "One" (*eka*).
KB_5.5.16: He thereby gratifies him alone. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.5.17: Moreover, "ka" is indeed a name for happiness.
KB_5.5.18: He thus bestows happiness upon himself. (The Cāturmāsya)
KB_5.5.19: Now, as for the fact that he gives a pair of cattle; KB_5.5.20: that is the form of procreation.
KB_5.5.21: Then, as for the fact that he sacrifices the *vājina* [oblation]; (The Cāturmāsya).
KB_5.5.22: Regarding these, the Brāhmaṇa has been stated.
KB_5.5.23: Now, as for the fact that he sacrifices to Varuṇa in the waters; KB_5.5.24: he thereby gratifies him in his own abode. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifices)

KB_5.5.25: Now, as for the fact that he sacrifices subsequently with the Full Moon sacrifice; KB_5.5.26: thus indeed his sacrifice has been performed with the Varuṇapraghāsa offerings during the bright fortnight. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.6.1:
This sacrificial rite, namely the Sākamedha, belongs to Indra.
KB_5.6.2: Just as a great king, having drawn up his armies in front, would follow a path free from fear; (Cāturmāsya) KB_5.6.3:
even so does he sacrifice to the deities in front. (Cāturmāsya) KB_5.6.4: Just as there is that great vow (*mahāvrata*) of Soma; (Cāturmāsya)
KB_5.6.5: In this very same way, this is the *iṣṭi* and the *mahāvratam*.
KB_5.6.6: Now, as for the fact that he first sacrifices to Agni Anīkavant among the deities—KB_5.6.7: Agni, indeed, is the mouth of the gods.
KB_5.6.8: By this very act, he gratifies the gods at the outset.
KB_5.6.9: Now, as for the fact that he sacrifices to the Maruts Sāṃtapana at midday— (Cāturmāsya) KB_5.6.10:
For it is at midday that [the sun] burns most intensely.
Therefore, at midday, he sacrifices to the Maruts Sāṃtapana. Furthermore, the Maruts belong to Indra,
and the midday pressing belongs to Indra.

KB_5.6.14: Therefore, at midday, he sacrifices to the Maruts Sāṃtapana. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice) KB_5.6.15: Now, as to why they perform the rite with the Gṛhamedhīya offering in the evening— KB_5.6.16: The Gṛhamedhīya is indeed a rite for nourishment. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice)
KB_5.6.17: [The offering] is the nourishment of the evening.
KB_5.6.18: Therefore, the two butter-portions (*ājyabhāga*) become possessed of nourishment.
KB_5.6.19: It thereby nourishes the sacrificer himself. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifices)

KB_5.6.20: Now, as for the fact that they perform the rite with the full ladle in the morning; KB_5.6.21: by means of the ritual of the previous day, he thus connects the morning ritual. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifices) KB_5.7.1:
Now, as for the Maruts Krīḍins whom he sacrifices to.
The Maruts are indeed the playmates of Indra;
therefore, he sacrifices to them while they are joined together with Indra. Now, as for why he sacrifices to Mahendra at the end.
KB_5.7.5: The merchant indeed enjoys the end.
KB_5.7.6: Therefore, he sacrifices for him at the end. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.7.7:
Now, as for the fact that they lead forward the fire or that it is churned, the Brāhmaṇa explanation for that has already been stated.

KB_5.7.8: Now, as for the fact that there are seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses, the two *ājyabhāga* offerings contain the word "sat," and the two *saṃyājyā* verses are *virāj*s—its *brāhmaṇa* explanation has already been stated. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.7.9:
Now, as for the fact that there are nine *prayāja*s, nine *anuyāja*s, eight oblations (*havīṃṣi*), and the *sviṣṭakṛt* offering as the ninth—(The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.7.10:
By this, one attains the *nakṣatriyā virāj*.

KB_5.7.11: There are six common *saṃcara* oblations, ending with the one for Indra and Agni, belonging to the Vāruṇapraghāsa [sacrifice]. (Cāturmāsya) KB_5.7.12: Their *brāhmaṇa* explanation has been stated. KB_5.7.13:
Now, as for the fact that he sacrifices to Mahendra, its *brāhmaṇa* explanation has been stated. (Cāturmāsya)
Now, as for the cake on one potsherd for Viśvakarman:
he who shines yonder is indeed Viśvakarman;
it is him that he thereby gratifies. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifices)

KB_5.7.17: Now, as for the fact that he gives a bull; KB_5.7.18: for this sacrificial rite belongs to Indra. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.8.1: Now, as for the fact that they proceed with the Pitṛyajña in the afternoon.
KB_5.8.2: The ancestors indeed partake of waning.

KB_5.8.3: Therefore, they perform the sacrifice to the ancestors in the afternoon. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.8.4: Regarding this they say: "Since the ancestors partake of the latter fortnight, why then does one sacrifice to them during the former fortnight? (The Cāturmāsya)

KB_5.8.5: Or these ancestors are divine. KB_5.8.6: Therefore, they sacrifice to them during the waxing moon. KB_5.8.7: Now, as for the fact that he recites one *sāmidhenī* verse [at each of the three *cāturmāsya* sacrifices]. (The Cāturmāsya)
KB_5.8.8: The ancestors, indeed, are as it were once-born. KB_5.8.9: Therefore, he recites one *sāmidhenī* verse.
KB_5.8.10: That [verse], moreover, is an *anuṣṭubh*. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice)
The Anuṣṭubh is speech. The ancestors, indeed, have departed; it is by means of this Anuṣṭubh verse, which is speech, that he causes them to come back. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice)
Now, as for why he does not recite the ancestral lineage (*ārṣeya*) of the sacrificer:
[it is] lest he should exclude the sacrificer. Then he recites this *nigada*; its *brāhmaṇa* has already been explained.

KB_5.8.17: Now, when he invokes [the Pitṛs] with the words, "Soma accompanied by the Pitṛs," or "the Pitṛs who possess Soma," "the Pitṛs seated on the sacrificial grass," or "the Pitṛs consumed by Agni"; KB_5.8.18: For these Pitṛs are indeed divine;
KB_5.8.19: therefore, he invokes them.
Now, as for why he invokes Agni Kavyavāhana:
the ancestors are indeed the Sviṣṭakṛt;
therefore, he invokes him.

KB_5.8.23: Some do not invoke their own greatness, saying, "This is the greatness of the sacrificer. KB_5.8.24: However, it is established that one should indeed invoke them. KB_5.8.25: For this is truly the greatness of Agni.
Now, as for why he omits the *barhis*-bearing fore-sacrifices (*prayāja*) and after-sacrifices (*anuyāja*):
the *barhis* is indeed offspring;
[he does this] thinking, "May I thus propagate offspring."
KB_5.8.29: These indeed become six. KB_5.8.30: There are six seasons. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.8.31: The seasons are the fathers.
KB_5.8.32: By that, he indeed gratifies the ancestors. KB_5.8.33:
Now, as for the fact that the two butter-portions (*ājyabhāga*) contain the word "living" (*jīvanavat*):
KB_5.8.34: By that, he indeed gives life to the sacrificer.
KB_5.8.35: Now, as for the fact that there are three portions each from one oblation; (Cāturmāsya) KB_5.8.36: There are indeed three oblations; KB_5.8.37:
he cuts off portions from them together.

Therefore, there are three [formulas] for each of the three oblations. Furthermore, by this act pertaining to the gods, he distinguishes the rite for the ancestors. Moreover, the ancestors have indeed gone to the furthest distance.
KB_5.8.41: He calls them with the first [formula]. (Cāturmāsya) KB_5.8.42: He causes them to come with the second.
KB_5.8.43: He sends them forth with the third. (Cāturmāsya)
KB_5.9.1: Now, as for the fact that he sacrifices to Agni Kavyavāhana at the end; KB_5.9.2: the ancestors are indeed the Sviṣṭakṛt;
KB_5.9.3: therefore, he sacrifices to him at the end. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifices)
KB_5.9.4: Now, as for the fact that he touches water, its Brāhmaṇa explanation has already been stated.
KB_5.9.5: Now, as for the fact that they do not eat the *iḍā* after having invoked it and smelled it— (Cāturmāsya) KB_5.9.6: The *iḍā* is indeed cattle.
KB_5.9.7: "Lest I deprive the sacrificer of his cattle," [he thinks].
KB_5.9.8: Now, when the Adhvaryu gives to the ancestors, KB_5.9.9: he thereby gratifies the ancestors themselves.

KB_5.9.10: Now, as for the fact that they purify themselves with the *pavitra* [strainers], its Brāhmaṇa explanation has already been stated. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.9.11: Now, as for the fact that they mutter a verse (*ṛc*), they thereby perform an act of securing well-being (*svastyayana*).
KB_5.9.12: Now, as for the fact that, having gone toward the north, they worship the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya fires. (The Cāturmāsya)
KB_5.9.13: Having indeed gratified them, they finally declare their purpose among the gods.
KB_5.9.14: Moreover, the sacrifice to the ancestors is generally concluded with the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). KB_5.9.15: They now make that very same [sacrifice] conclude toward the north.
KB_5.9.16: Now, as for the fact that they go out toward the east and worship the sun; KB_5.9.17: The sun is indeed the world of the gods;
KB_5.9.18: The fathers are the world of the ancestors.
KB_5.9.19: Thus they ascend from the world of the ancestors to the world of the gods. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice) KB_5.9.20:
Now, as for the fact that he does not utter the name of the sacrificer in the *sūktavāka*— KB_5.9.21: [It is] so that he does not exclude the sacrificer. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice)

KB_5.9.22: Now, as for the fact that they do not perform the *patnīsaṃyāja* offerings—it is so that the wives shall not be excluded from the ritual. KB_5.9.23: And as for the fact that, having gone toward the north, they perform the *tryambaka* offerings—(this pertains to the Cāturmāsya). KB_5.9.24: [End of section].
KB_5.9.25: Thus they gratify Rudra himself in his own quarter. (Cāturmāsya) KB_5.9.26:
Moreover, the sacrifice to the ancestors (pitṛyajña) is indeed performed from south to north. KB_5.9.27: They thus make it proceed from east to west. (Cāturmāsya)
Now, as for the fact that he performs an *iṣṭi* sacrifice at the end:
these Sākamedha offerings indeed constitute the conclusion; therefore, he performs an *iṣṭi* sacrifice at the end. (The Cāturmāsya)

KB_5.9.31: Now, when he subsequently sacrifices with the Full Moon sacrifice; (Cāturmāsya) KB_5.9.32: thus indeed his sacrifice with the Sākamedha offerings has been performed during the bright fortnight. (Cāturmāsya) KB_5.10.1: Or rather, he attains this thirteenth month when he sacrifices with the Śunāsīrya.
KB_5.10.2: This thirteenth month is indeed the entirety of the year. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.10.3: Thus, in this very [month], the entire year becomes attained.
KB_5.10.4: Now, as for the fact that he sacrifices to Śunāsīrau. (The Cāturmāsya)
Peace is indeed the remedy; [the words] "The two furrows are ploughed by the dog" constitute that peace.

This very peace, as a remedy, is performed at the conclusion of the sacrifice. (The Cāturmāsya) If fire is churned, that which is the ritual procedure (*tantra*) of the Vaiśvadeva is the ritual procedure for this as well.

KB_5.10.8: If, however, it is not churned, the Full Moon sacrifice alone constitutes the ritual framework (*tantra*). (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.10.9: The Full Moon sacrifice is indeed a firm foundation; it is for the sake of stability. KB_5.10.10:

Now, as for the seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses, the two *ājyabhāga* offerings containing the word "sat," and the two *saṃyājyā* verses in the *virāj* meter—the *brāhmaṇa* explanation for these has already been stated. (The Cāturmāsya)

KB_5.10.11: Now, as for the nine *prayāja*s, the nine *anuyāja*s, the eight oblations (*havīṃṣi*), and the *sviṣṭakṛt* as the ninth—KB_5.10.12: thereby one attains the Virāj consisting of the lunar mansions (*nakṣatriyā*). KB_5.10.13: However, the five recurring oblations (*saṃcarāṇi havīṃṣi*) remain the same, ending with that for Pūṣan, belonging to the Vaiśvadeva [parvan].
Regarding these, the Brāhmaṇa has been stated. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifice) KB_5.10.15:
Now, as for the fact that he sacrifices to Śuna and Sīra—KB_5.10.16:
regarding those two, the Brāhmaṇa has been stated.
Now, as for the fact that he sacrifices to Vāyu:
Vāyu is indeed the breath; thus, he places breath within himself. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifices)
Now, as for the cake on one potsherd for Sūrya: that which shines yonder is indeed Sūrya; it is him he thereby gratifies. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifices)
KB_5.10.23: Now, as for the white sacrificial fee;
KB_5.10.24: it is this very one that he thereby gratifies; KB_5.10.25: its form is thus produced. (The Cāturmāsya Sacrifices)
Now, when they perform substitutes for expiations or offer oblations,
they thereby effect a means of well-being;
it is for the sake of the pacification of the sacrifice.

KB_5.10.29: And for the healing of the sacrificer. (The Cāturmāsya) KB_5.10.30: Now, as to why they consecrate the sacrificer with his own fires. KB_5.10.31: The fires are indeed the chariot of the gods. (The Cāturmāsya)
KB_5.10.32: They place him upon that very divine chariot.
KB_5.10.33: By means of this divine chariot, he goes to the heavenly world.
KB_5.10.34: Where the world of the doers of good deeds is, where the world of the doers of good deeds is. (The Cāturmāsya)
Prajāpati, desiring offspring, performed austerities. From him, having thus performed austerities, five were born.
(Zūlagava: Brahmanhood)
KB_6.1.3: Agni, Vāyu, Āditya, Candramas, and Uṣas as the fifth;
KB_6.1.4: He said to them, "You too must perform penance. KB_6.1.5: They consecrated themselves.
While they were consecrated and performing penance, Uṣas, having assumed the form of an Apsaras belonging to Prajāpati, rose up before them.
In that [state], their mind fell into union.
They shed semen.
They said to Prajāpati, their father: "It is yours."
"Let us pour forth seed; may it not be lost upon us.
KB_6.1.11: Prajāpati made a golden cup, one arrow's length high and likewise across.
In that [soma], he poured this [seed] together.
From that, he arose as the thousand-eyed, thousand-footed one.
KB_6.1.14: With a thousand [cows] presented as a gift;
KB_6.1.15: He approached his father Prajāpati.
He said to him, "Why do you press me?
He replied, "Give me a name."
KB_6.1.18: "I shall not eat this food with a name that has not been prescribed. KB_6.2.1: He said, "You are indeed he," [to which the other replied] "Become [Bhava] indeed."
KB_6.2.2: By that which is "bhava-āpaḥ" (the waters of existence), [he is protected].
KB_6.2.3: Existence (*bhava*) does not indeed harm him.
KB_6.2.4: Neither his offspring, nor his cattle, nor even one who speaks against him is harmed.
(Regarding the *Zūlagava*: the office of the Brahman priest) KB_6.2.5:
Now, whoever hates him; KB_6.2.6:
he alone becomes the worse off.
KB_6.2.7: He who knows thus [attains this]. KB_6.2.8: His vow is that he should wear only a wet garment; he should not look upon water.
He pursued him for a second time.
He said to him, "Why do you pursue me?"
"Give me a second name," he said. "I shall not eat food under this single name alone."
"He is indeed you," he said; "He is Śarva.
"Insofar as Śarva is Agni, by that [name]."
Indeed, Śarva does not harm him;
he harms neither his offspring, nor his cattle, nor even one who speaks against him.
KB_6.2.17: Now, he who hates him— KB_6.2.18: he alone becomes worse off.
KB_6.2.19: He who knows this thus. KB_6.2.20: His vow is that he should not eat anything at all.
(The Brahmanhood of the Zūlagava sacrifice)
He stretched out toward that third one.
He said to him, "Why do you stretch out toward me?
(The Bull: On the Role of the Brahman Priest)
"Give me a third name," he said. "I will not eat food under two names," he replied.
"You are indeed Paśupati (Lord of Cattle)," he said.
KB_6.2.26: Because Vāyu is the Lord of Cattle, by that [reason].
KB_6.2.27: Indeed, the Lord of Cattle does not harm him.
KB_6.2.28: He destroys his offspring, his cattle, and even his reputation. KB_6.2.29: But he who hates him [destroys] himself.
He alone becomes more sinful;
he who knows thus does not. (The office of the Brahman priest at the Zūlagava sacrifice)
KB_6.2.32: His vow is that he must not revile a Brāhmaṇa. KB_6.2.33: He bestowed that fourth [portion] upon him. (The office of Brahman priest at the Zūlagava sacrifice)
He said to him, "Why do you press me?
He replied, "Give me a fourth name.
(The Bull of the Zūla; the office of Brahman)
KB_6.2.36: "I shall not eat this food with three names.
KB_6.2.37: "It is indeed you," he said; "the fierce one, O god.
(The Brahmanhood of the Zūlagava)
KB_6.2.38: Because the fierce god, the plants, and the trees [are present] therein;
KB_6.2.39: indeed, the fierce god does not harm him. (The office of the Brahman priest at the Zūlagava sacrifice)
KB_6.2.40: Neither his offspring, nor his cattle, nor even his reputation shall remain;
KB_6.2.41: rather, he who hates him [shall suffer]. (The office of the Brahman priest at the *Zūlagava* sacrifice)
KB_6.2.42: He indeed becomes more evil.
KB_6.2.43: Not so for him who knows thus.
KB_6.2.44: His vow is that he should not look into the private parts of a woman.
He stretched toward him for the fifth time.
He said to him, "Why do you stretch toward me?"
"Give me a fifth name," he said. "I shall not eat food under these four names alone."
"Truly, you are that," he said; "you are indeed the great deity. Because he is the great deity Āditya, therefore [he is so called].
The Great God does not indeed harm him;
he harms neither his offspring, nor his cattle, nor even one who speaks against him.
(Regarding the *Zūlagava*: the office of the Brahman priest) KB_6.3.9:
Now, whoever hates him; KB_6.3.10:
he alone becomes worse off.
KB_6.3.11: He who knows this thus [attains success]. KB_6.3.12: His vow is that he should not look at the sun as it is rising, nor as it is setting.
He seized that sixth one.
He said to him, "Why do you seize me?"
"Give me a sixth name," he said. "I shall not eat food under five names," he replied.
"Indeed, you are he," he said; "Rudra indeed," [he replied]. "Insofar as Rudra is the moon, by that [he is]."
Rudra does not indeed harm him;
nor his offspring, nor his cattle, nor even one who speaks against him.
(The Brahmanhood of the Zūlagava)
KB_6.3.21: Now, he who hates him— KB_6.3.22: he alone becomes worse off;
KB_6.3.23: not he who knows thus.
KB_6.3.24: His vow is that he must not eat anything decomposed, nor marrow.
KB_6.3.25: He bestowed that [vow] as the seventh.
He said to him, "Why do you press me?
He replied, "Give me a seventh name."
"Indeed, I shall not eat this food with six names," he said.
"It is you indeed," he replied, "for you are the Lord."
KB_6.3.30: [He should offer] with the verse "Since Īśāna [is the eater], by that [food]";
KB_6.3.31: "Indeed, Īśāna does not harm him."
KB_6.3.32: He shall have neither offspring, nor cattle, nor even anyone who speaks on his behalf. KB_6.3.33: But he who hates him [shall suffer].
He alone becomes worse;
he does not [become worse] who knows thus.
(The Brahmanhood of the Zūlagava)
KB_6.3.36: His vow is this: "One should not refuse food even to one who desires it.
KB_6.3.37: He (the father) pressed him (the son) for the eighth part [of his property].

"Let my breath be consecrated by breath," with this he recites the third [verse].
He mentions the breath in the middle,
for this breath is indeed in the middle.
"May my eye be consecrated by the eye," with these words he performs the fourth [offering]. (Soma:
Dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭi) "May my hearing be consecrated by the ear," with these words he performs the fifth.
"Indeed, he consecrates those deities that reside within the person;
(in the Soma initiation sacrifice) no additional oblations are offered."
KB_7.6.23: Now, indeed, faith alone is the imperishability of that which has been once offered.
(Soma: Dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭi) KB_7.6.24: He who, being full of faith, performs the sacrifice—
KB_7.6.25: His sacrifice does not perish. KB_7.6.26: Water is imperishability.
(Soma: Dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭi)
KB_7.6.27: Those [deities] which are in these worlds and those which are here with respect to the self;
KB_7.6.28: he who, knowing them as the imperishable [essence] consisting of water, performs the sacrifice.
(Soma: Dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭi)
KB_7.6.29: His sacrifice does not perish.
KB_7.6.30: Keśin Dārbhya indeed proclaimed this very same inexhaustibility of that which is sacrificed once to the golden bird Hiraṇmaya.
(Soma: Dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭi)
KB_7.6.31: He undergoes initiation in the afternoon.
KB_7.6.32: For in the afternoon, indeed, he gathers all beings together.
(The Soma Initiation Offering)
Indeed, kings even pass him by;
therefore, when the sun sets as if toward the red [west],
[he performs the *dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭi*].
Indeed, one who undergoes initiation initiates himself into this very [Ātman].
In that he undergoes initiation in the afternoon,
it is for the attainment of all desires.
(Regarding the *dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭi*):

By means of the *prāyaṇīya* [offering], the gods attained the out-breath (*prāṇa*); by means of the *udayanīya* [offering], they attained the up-breath (*udāna*). In the same way, the sacrificer now attains the out-breath by means of the *prāyaṇīya*, and the up-breath by means of the *udayanīya*.
These two, the *prāyaṇīya* and the *udayanīya* offerings, are indeed the out-breath (*prāṇa*) and the up-breath (*udāna*). Therefore,
those who are the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) of the *prāyaṇīya* should also be the officiating priests of the *udayanīya*.
(Regarding the Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi):
For these two, the prāṇa and udāna breaths, are identical.
Indeed, having set out toward the heavenly world by means of the Prāyaṇīya sacrifice, the gods did not know the directions.
Agni said to them:
"Offer one oblation of clarified butter to me; I shall reveal one direction."
Therefore they offered oblations;
he perceived the eastern direction.
Therefore, they lead the fire forward;
the sacrifice is performed facing the east.
KB_7.7.13: Sitting facing eastward, they offer oblations into him. KB_7.7.14:
For this is his well-known direction.
(The Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi of the Soma sacrifice)
Then Soma said:
"Offer one oblation of clarified butter for me; I shall make one of the quarters known.
(The Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
KB_7.7.17: Therefore, they offered oblations. KB_7.7.18: He perceived the southern direction. KB_7.7.19: Therefore, they carry the purchased Soma toward the south.
KB_7.7.20: Standing to the south, he recites the invitatory verses.
(The Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi of the Soma sacrifice) KB_7.7.21:
Standing to the south, he performs the concluding verses.
KB_7.7.22: They press him while sitting toward the south alone.
KB_7.7.23: For this direction of his is well-known.
Then Savitṛ said:
"Offer one oblation of clarified butter for me; I shall discern one direction.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
KB_7.7.26: Therefore, they offered oblations.
KB_7.7.27: He perceived the western direction. KB_7.7.28: That is indeed Savitṛ, who shines yonder.
Therefore, they see him going westward day after day, not eastward;
for this is his well-known direction.
Then Pathyā Svasti said:
"Offer one oblation of clarified butter for me; I shall discern one direction."
They offered oblations for that [offering];
it recognized the northern direction.
Speech is indeed the path and well-being.
Therefore, in the northern direction, speech is uttered most clearly.
KB_7.7.37: They go upward indeed to learn the sacred word.
KB_7.7.38: Or whoever comes from that [place].
"Indeed, they desire to hear him," so it is said.
For this is the well-known direction of speech.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
Then Aditi said:
"Offer one oblation of food for me; I shall discern one of the directions.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
They offered oblations to her.
She perceived the upward direction.
This earth, indeed, is Aditi.
Therefore, on this [earth], plants rise upwards, trees rise upwards, and human beings rise upwards.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
The fire blazes upwards. Whatever there is above this earth is dependent upon that very [fire].
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
For this is the well-known direction for it.
Thus indeed did the gods, by means of the *prāyaṇīya* [offering], perceive the heavenly world. (The *Prāyaṇīya* Sacrifice)
In the same way, it is thus that the sacrificer, by means of the *prāyaṇīya* [offering] itself, comes to know the world of heaven. (Soma:
*Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi*) Those two, the *prāyaṇīya* and the *udayanīya*, should be equal.
This sacrifice is indeed the chariot of the gods;
its two wings are the Prāyaṇīya and Udayanīya offerings.
KB_7.8.15: He who makes them equal.
(The Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi of the Soma sacrifice) KB_7.8.16:
Just as one driving on a road with a chariot that has wheels on both sides and powerful draft-animals might reach a destination where he had not intended to go.
(Regarding the *prāyaṇīyeṣṭi* sacrifice:
Thus, he attains the world of heaven with well-being. Now, as for him who acts otherwise [in an uneven manner], [he does not attain it].
Just as one driving a chariot with wings on only one side, drawn by fierce horses, might not reach his destination when the road is uneven.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
In this way, he does not attain the auspicious world of heaven. Therefore, the *prāyaṇīya* and *udayanīya* offerings should be equal.
(The *Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi*)
KB_7.9.1: The Prāyaṇīya [offering] concludes with the *śamyu*-formula; the Udayanīya concludes with the *śamyu*-formula.
KB_7.9.2: At the Prāyaṇīya, he sacrifices first to Pathyā Svasti.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
KB_7.9.3: Then [he offers] to Agni, then to Soma, then to Savitṛ, then to Aditi. KB_7.9.4:
By means of the introductory sacrifice (*prāyaṇīyeṣṭi*), one indeed approaches the heavenly world.
(Soma: *Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi*)
KB_7.9.5: In that he offers the Pathyā Svasti first, KB_7.9.6: he thereby effects a journey for well-being, for the attainment of the heavenly world.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
KB_7.9.7: At the Udayanīya sacrifice, he offers to Agni first.
KB_7.9.8: Then to Soma, then to Savitṛ, then to Pathyā Svasti, and then to Aditi.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīya-iṣṭi)
KB_7.9.9: By means of the *udayanīyā* offering, one returns to this world. KB_7.9.10: Therefore, he sacrifices to Pathyā Svasti at the conclusion.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
He thereby effects a blessing for the attainment of this world.
He indeed sacrifices to those five deities.
(The Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi of Soma)
KB_7.9.13: By means of them, one obtains whatever fivefold [entity] there is, whether it pertains to the deities (*adhidaivata*) or to the self (*adhyātma*).
KB_7.9.14: These are their *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
KB_7.9.15: These [verses] indeed contain words for "well-being" (*svasti*), "path," "completion," "descent," and "leading.
(The Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi) KB_7.9.16:

The Maruts are indeed the subjects of the gods, whose domain is the intermediate space; they are capable of making the sacrifice of the sacrificer one that is beautiful in form as it departs toward the heavenly world.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi) KB_7.9.17:
Now, as for the fact that [the verses] contain the word *svasti*, the word *pathin*, the word *pari*, the word *pra*, and the word *ni*.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
KB_7.9.18: The Maruts, the divine hosts, do not harm him. KB_7.9.19: He attains the heavenly world in safety.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
He indeed reverses them:
those which are the *puronuvākyās* at the introductory offering (*prāyaṇīyā*), he makes the *yājyās* at the concluding offering (*udayanīyā*);
those which are the *yājyās*, he makes the *puronuvākyās*.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi) One who proceeds with the Prāyaṇīya [offering] indeed departs from this world.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
When that [breath] reverses,
it becomes established in this world;
that is, in its firm foundation, without falling away.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi) KB_7.10.8:
Moreover, the meters are indeed the vital breaths; KB_7.10.9:
he thus interweaves the vital breaths within himself for the sake of non-separation.

Therefore, these vital breaths, though emitted in all directions, do not escape. "Thee, O most glorious one, that which is most effective," and "This for Agni"— these two *anuṣṭubh* verses are the *saṃyājyās*.
The Prāyaṇīya offering is indeed the beginning of the sacrifice;
the Anuṣṭubh is speech.
The sacrifice is performed by means of speech;
one does not transpose these two.
The two *saṃyājyā* verses are indeed the foundation. [He thinks:
"Lest I intermingle these two foundations.
(Soma: Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi)
It comes to a conclusion;
that is the form for advancing. Just as one might dwell in the vicinity of heaven when approaching it, so it is with that.
(Regarding the *prāyaṇīyeṣṭi*):
Because it concludes with the *śamyu*-formula,
indeed all the deities assemble at the *prāyaṇīya*.
(Regarding the *prāyaṇīyeṣṭi* sacrifice: KB_7.11.6:
If one were to perform the *saṃyājana* offerings at this point, KB_7.11.7:
it would be as if one were to lead the wives of the gods toward a great multitude that has already gathered; such would it be.
(Regarding the Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi: KB 7.11.8: If someone were to say of him there:
"He has approached the wives of the gods, who are a multitude that has come together," [he would be at fault]. KB 7.11.9: [The same applies if he approaches them] while they are already assembled.
(Regarding the Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi:
"His wife will enter the assembly hall"—so it may indeed be.
Therefore, the sacrifice concludes with the *śamyu* formula.
For the non-conflict with the deities; (Soma:
Prāyaṇīyeṣṭi).
In this direction— the one that is north-east— the Asuras hemmed in the gods. While remaining in that direction, they consecrated Soma for kingship.
With Soma as their king, they drove the Asuras away from these worlds.
In the same way, the sacrificer now drives his hateful rivals away from these worlds by means of Soma as king.
(On the purchase of Soma) KB_7.12.1: He indeed purchases it with four things: with a cow, with gold, with a garment, and with a she-goat.
KB_7.12.2: For a pair consisting of four items is a productive couple, for the sake of procreation.
Now, that King Soma is indeed the far-seeing moon.
He enters this very [Soma] as one already purchased. Therefore, he purchases King Soma. (The Purchase of Soma)
KB_7.12.6: "Yonder King Soma, the far-seeing moon, has been pressed.
KB_7.12.7: For that purchased [Soma], he recites nine verses.
(The Purchase of Soma)
These vital breaths are nine. He thereby places the vital breaths in the sacrificer, for the sake of reaching a full lifespan in this world.
"For immortality, to yonder world" (KB_7.12.11);
"From good he goes toward better" (KB_7.12.12)— he recites these verses beginning with a downward slope for one who is being led down the slope.
"May Bṛhaspati be your forerunner," he says.
Bṛhaspati is indeed the sacred formulation (*brahman*).
KB_7.12.15: For the attainment of the glory of Brahman.
(Soma: Soma-purchase) KB_7.12.16:
He recites two Triṣṭubh verses addressed to Varuṇa: "O God, this prayer of one who strives," and "In the forests he has spread across the atmosphere."
The Triṣṭubh is indeed the kṣatra;
Varuṇa is the kṣatra.
KB_7.12.19: For the attainment of the glory of the *kṣatra*.
KB_7.12.20: He recites four *gāyatrī* verses addressed to Soma, beginning with "O Soma, those [drops] of thine which are delightful."
The Gāyatrī is indeed Brahman;
Soma is the Kṣatra.
KB_7.12.23: For the attainment of the glory of the Brahmin and the glory of the Kṣatriya.
(Soma: Soma-purchase) KB_7.12.24:
Having recited the second half-verse of the last of those [verses], he stops.
The Ṛg-verse is indeed immortality;
he enters that immortality.
(Soma: the purchase of Soma)
Now, the *ṛc* is indeed Brahman.
Thus, on both sides, he makes the two half-verses of the *ṛc* his armor, [thereby protecting] the Brahman.
(Soma: the purchase of Soma)
KB_7.12.29: Wherever he might stop with a half-verse, that is indeed a Brāhmaṇa passage. KB_7.12.30:

"Those abodes of yours which they worship with oblation"—this verse beginning with *pra* he recites for one who is about to enter the water. KB_7.12.31: "Those abodes of yours which they worship with oblation"—this verse beginning with *pra* he recites for one who is about to enter the water.

With the verse containing the word "arrived" (*āgatavatī*) and the word "seasons" (*ṛtumati*), namely, "The god has arrived; may he increase the dwelling with the seasons," he performs the concluding dedication.
"Soma the King is indeed the year," so said Kauṣītaki.
"He approaches together with the seasons as he comes. (The Purchase of Soma)
He recites verses that are appropriate;
for whatever is appropriate in the sacrifice is successful, and this is for the success of the sacrifice itself.
(Soma: the purchase of Soma)
He recites those nine [verses]. Their Brāhmaṇa explanation has been stated.
By repeating the first and the last [verses] three times each, they amount to thirteen.
The year consists of twelve months;
[this is] for the attainment of the year itself.
There is a thirteenth month;
its ritual designation is as if well-known for the sake of its attainment, for the sake of its attainment.
(Soma: the purchase of Soma)

By means of the guest-offering (*ātithya*), the gods indeed obtained both two-footed and four-footed cattle. In the same way, by means of this very guest-offering, the sacrificer obtains both two-footed and four-footed cattle.
(Soma: Churning of the Fire)
KB_8.1.3: When the guest-offering of sacrificial food is near at hand, they churn the fire.
KB_8.1.4: For this guest-offering is indeed the head of the sacrifice.
(Soma: Churning of the Fire)
KB_8.1.5: Breath is Agni. KB_8.1.6: He thereby places that breath in the head. KB_8.1.7: He recites twelve verses for kindling the fire.
Twelve indeed are the months of the year;
[it is performed] for the attainment of the year itself.
KB_8.1.10: He recites the first [verse] dedicated to Savitṛ: "O God Savitṛ, toward you... (Soma: churning of the fire).
KB_8.1.11: This is for the sake of being impelled by Savitṛ.

KB_8.1.12: "For one impelled by Savitṛ, indeed, no harm whatsoever occurs; it is for the sake of safety. KB_8.1.13: He recites the verse addressed to Heaven and Earth, beginning with "May the great Heaven and Earth... for the sake of Heaven and Earth.

Heaven and earth are indeed the two supports; [he recites this] for the sake of support. "Thee, O Agni, from the lotus-leaf," with these three verses he recites after [the fire] has been churned out for one who is being churned.

KB_8.1.16: [He recites] "And let the people speak" with the *jātavatī* verse for the fire that has been produced. KB_8.1.17: [He recites] "Him, who is held in the hand like a ring" with the *hastavatī* verse for the fire being held by the hand.
"Forward to the god for the feast of the gods"— this [verse] ending in "pra" is for the fire being carried forward;
"To him who is born in Jātavedas"— this [verse] ending in "ā" is for the fire being summoned.
(Agni-manthana) KB_8.1.20:
"By fire is fire kindled; for you, O Agni, are kindled by fire"—these two verses containing the word *samiddha* are for the fire being kindled.
(Soma: Agni-manthana)
KB_8.1.21: He concludes with the verse, "They groom him, the one of good wisdom," ending with the line, "the vigorous one in his own dwellings.
(Soma: Churning of the Fire) KB_8.1.22:
For "dwellings" (*kṣaya*) is indeed the end.
KB_8.1.23: [The verse] ending with the *paridhānīyā*. KB_8.1.24: He places the end at the end.
(Soma: Churning of the Fire)
KB_8.2.1: With this [verse], one also [proceeds] here and during the Cāturmāsya sacrifices.
KB_8.2.2: By repeating the first [verse] three times and the last [verse] three times, they amount to sixteen [recitations].
(Soma: Churning of the Fire)
KB_8.2.3: Or all this consists of sixteen parts.
KB_8.2.4: It is for the attainment of all this very thing.
KB_8.2.5: Now, where the animal is sacrificed—
Having recited this [verse] in its direct order—"The gods sacrificed with the sacrifice"—he concludes with a Triṣṭubh verse.
(Soma: Churning of the Fire)
The cattle are connected with the *triṣṭubh* meter; [this is] for the attainment of cattle. By repeating the first verse three times and the last verse three times, they amount to seventeen.
(Soma: Churning of the Fire)
Prajāpati is indeed seventeenfold. This is indeed the successful dharma that is commensurate with Prajāpati.
(Soma: Churning of the Fire)
He recites seventeen *sāmidhenī* verses.
Prajāpati is indeed seventeenfold. This is the successful rite, namely that which is commensurate with Prajāpati.
(Soma: The Guest-Offering) KB_8.2.14:
The two butter-portions (*ājyabhāga*) are [recited with] the *vārtraghna* verses, for the very purpose of slaying evil. KB_8.2.15:
Furthermore, thus his ritual procedure (*tantra*) is not displaced from the full-moon sacrifice.
(Soma: *Ātithyeṣṭi*) KB_8.2.16:
Some perform [the offering] with two verses containing the word "guest" (*atithi*).
KB_8.2.17: However, the two *vārtraghna* verses remain fixed [as the standard].
KB_8.2.18: "The *ṛc* and the *yājyā* should be [identical]," so some say.
(Regarding the *Soma* sacrifice: the *Ātithyeṣṭi*) KB_8.2.19:
Others say, "In the *upasads*, these deities have *ṛc*s as their *yājyās*."
KB_8.2.20: However, the two *yājyā* verses remain as those beginning with *juṣāṇa*.
(Soma: *Ātithyeṣṭi*) KB_8.2.21:
He offers the sacrifice with the verse, "O Viṣṇu, [to] Soma who is present... (*somam santam viṣṇo*).
KB_8.2.22: When he who has been purchased enters here as it were;
KB_8.2.23: that indeed is his form belonging to Viṣṇu; KB_8.2.24:
and because he sacrifices with the formula "Viṣṇu," while [the Soma] is actually Soma.
(Regarding the *Soma-Ātithyeṣṭi*):
By the name "Viṣṇu," he is indeed the eater;
by the name "Soma," he is the one to be eaten.

Therefore, those who say "Soma," offer oblations and consume [the portion] in this manner. The invitatory verse (*puronuvākyā*) and the offering verse (*yājyā*) for the oblation are both in the *triṣṭubh* meter.
The Triṣṭubh is indeed strength and vigor.
Thus, he bestows that very strength and vigor upon the sacrificer.
(Soma: Aātithya-iṣṭi)

KB_8.3.1: "The Hotṛ of the sacrifice with the bright chariot, he who has good horses and fine gold, O Agni..."—these two *saṃyājyā* verses, containing the word "guest" (*atithi*) and the word "chariot" (*ratha*), are in the *triṣṭubh* meter and dedicated to Agni.
(Soma: *Ātithya-iṣṭi*).
KB_8.3.2: Just as that is fourfold-perfect, so is this.
KB_8.3.3: For him who performs these [rites], the chariot becomes as it were a mere atom.
(Soma: Aitihya-iṣṭi) KB_8.3.4: It concludes with the *iḍā*.
That is the form for advancing.
Just as one might dwell in a place that is close to heaven, so it is with this.
(The Soma: *Ātithyeṣṭi*)
KB_8.3.7: At the Upāṃśu-sacrifice, these offerings take place: the Dīkṣaṇīyā, the Prāyaṇīyā, the Ātithyeṣṭi, and the Upasads.
(Soma: Ātithyeṣṭi) KB_8.3.8: Indeed, these offerings constitute the emission of semen.
KB_8.3.9: Indeed, the seed is discharged silently.
KB_8.3.10: They proceed while relinquishing their ritual duties.
(Soma: Aātithya-iṣṭi)
KB_8.3.11: The Dīkṣaṇīyā [offering] ends with the Patnīsaṃyāja. KB_8.3.12: The Prāyaṇīyā [offering] ends with the Śamyu-formula. KB_8.3.13: The Ātithyā [offering] ends with the Iḍā.
(Soma: *Ātithyeṣṭi*) KB_8.3.14: He offers the *pratiyājā* sacrifices during the *devatopasthāna*.
KB_8.3.15: By means of these rites, Prajāpati indeed went to the heavenly world through the act of renunciation (*utsarga*).
In the same way, the sacrificer goes to the heavenly world by means of these very rites as his departure.
(Soma: Atithyā-iṣṭi)
The Mahāvīra vessel is indeed the head of the sacrifice.
One should not prepare it at one's first sacrifice.
However, the subsequent sacrifice becomes inclined toward him who does not prepare it at his first sacrifice.
KB_8.4.4: However, one may perform the *pravargya* for anyone who is learned in the Vedas (*anūcāna*) and a *śrotriya*.
KB_8.4.5: For he is indeed the self of the sacrifice.
By means of his own self, he thus brings the sacrifice to completion. Now,
that which shines yonder is indeed the Mahāvīra.
By this, he gratifies him alone.
He should recite the hymn of praise for him with one hundred and one verses.
KB_8.4.10: Indeed, this [sun] shines when placed at a distance of a hundred *yojanas*.
KB_8.4.11: By means of that very hundred [of bricks], he traverses that path of a hundred *yojanas*.
Now, that which is the one hundred and first [brick] is the world of the sacrificer. The sacrificer attains this very self.
KB_8.4.14: That person whom they declare to be in the sun; KB_8.4.15: he is Indra, he is Prajāpati, he is Brahman.
KB_8.4.16: In this very [rite], the sacrificer attains co-residence (*salokatā*) and union (*sāyujya*) with all the deities.
KB_8.5.1: He should recite the hymn without taking breath, for the continuity of the vital breaths (*prāṇa*).
For these vital breaths are, as it were, continuous. One should recite the loud, explicit praise.
(Soma: Pravargya)
The *stubha* is indeed the vital breaths;
for it is manifest,
and its deity is speech.
KB_8.5.7: He first recites the Sāvitrī verses.
KB_8.5.8: This is for the sake of being impelled by Savitṛ.
KB_8.5.9: Indeed, for one impelled by Savitṛ, no harm whatsoever occurs; [this is] for the sake of safety.
(Soma: Pravargya) KB_8.5.10: "The Brahman, born first in the east... [he recites].
KB_8.5.11: This indeed is the Brahman born first in the east;
(Soma: Pravargya) KB_8.5.12:
where yonder sun shines.
KB_8.5.13: That very [verse] establishes the sacrificer. KB_8.5.14:

He recites two suitable verses—one containing the word "anointed" (*akta*) and the other containing the word "seated" (*sanna*)—over [the Mahāvīra vessel]: "Him whom the sages anoint as if spreading him out," and "Sit down;
thou art great. (Soma: Pravargya)
