"Away with the people! (*apeto janyam*)?
"O slayer of Vṛtra, fear born of others has been warded off;
they have turned away," [he says] as the Soma-carts move forward.
KB_9.4.16: Therefore, there is no transgression against those who have performed [the sacrifice].
KB_9.4.17: Consequently, from that very portion, fearlessness arises for him.
(Soma: The Moving Forward of the Havirdhāna Carts)
KB_9.4.18: Facing east, he should lean toward the northern track of the southern *havirdhāna* cart.
(Soma: the movement of the *havirdhāna*) KB_9.4.19: This world, indeed, is the southern *havirdhāna*.
KB_9.4.20: This world is indeed a firm foundation. KB_9.4.21: "May I proceed without severing myself from this foundation," [he thinks].
KB_9.4.22: Where he stands while reciting the *paridhānīyā* [verse], (regarding the moving forward of the *havirdhāna* carts), KB_9.4.26:
"It will fall," so it would indeed be.
KB_9.4.27: Therefore, having put on [the garment] and crossed over with his right arm [extended], he restrains his speech and returns by the same way he came.
(Soma: Moving the Havirdhāna Carts) KB_9.4.28: At the place where, while standing, he had previously spoken [the formula].
KB_9.4.29: Having stood there, he performs the casting of the fire. KB_9.4.30: Then he should approach the dwelling as before. (Soma: the moving forward of the *havirdhāna* shed)
Agni is indeed the *brahman*, and Soma is the *kṣatra*.
Therefore, when they lead forth Agni and Soma on the day of preparation (*upavasatha*),
they strike away the evil of the sacrificer by means of the *brahman* and the *kṣatra*.
Regarding this, they say: the Hotṛ should recite this first [verse] while sitting.
For indeed, all beings follow after King Soma as he is being led forth.
When the Hotṛ priest, sitting down, recites this verse,
he thereby brings all beings under control, each according to its proper abode.
"O God, impel [the sacrifice] for the first father," with these words he recites the Sāvitrī verse first.
(Soma: Agni-Soma Praṇayana)
KB_9.5.9: For the sake of being impelled by Savitṛ.
KB_9.5.10: Indeed, for one impelled by Savitṛ, no harm whatsoever occurs; [this is] for the sake of safety. (Soma: The Leading-forth of Agni and Soma)

KB_9.5.11: With the verse, "Arise, O Brahmanaspati," he causes [the fire] to rise; with the verse, "May Brahmanaspati go forth," he leads it forward; he recites two verses appropriate to Brahmanaspati. (Soma: The Leading Forth of Agni and Soma) KB_9.5.12: Brahmanaspati is indeed the Brahman.
KB_9.5.13: By means of the *brahman* alone, he thus brings that *brahman* to fulfillment.
(Soma: The Leading Forth of Agni and Soma) KB_9.5.14:
The Hotṛ recites two triplets dedicated exclusively to Agni, beginning with "The immortal god, O Agni" and "Up to thee, O Agni, day by day."
(Soma: The Leading Forth of Agni and Soma) KB_9.5.15:
For they lead Agni forth first. KB_9.5.16:
These two [mantras] indeed contain the word "iti."
KB_9.5.17: He praises the fire as it is being carried forward.
(Soma: *agnīṣomapraṇayana*) KB_9.5.18:
When he reaches [the spot], he says, "Place the embryo of beings."
KB_9.5.19: For one who desires a fetus, he should meditate upon a fetus [within the fire]. KB_9.5.20: She indeed obtains a fetus.
KB_9.5.21: Then they place the fire in the Āgnīdhra shed.
KB_9.5.22: Thereupon the Adhvaryu offers an oblation. (Soma: The Leading Forth of Agni and Soma)
KB_9.5.23: One should recite this [verse] over her: "O Agni, enjoy it; O Lord, take pleasure in that word.
KB_9.5.24: This is its *yājyā* verse: "Enjoy it; take pleasure in it," which is appropriate.
(Soma: the leading forth of Agni and Soma)
KB_9.6.1: Then they carry the Soma alone toward the east.
KB_9.6.2: Therefore, he recites the verses addressed to Soma alone. (The leading forth of Agni and Soma)
KB_9.6.3: Reciting the triplet beginning with "Soma comes, the finder of the way," he follows after [the Soma].
KB_9.6.4: Then the Adhvaryu offers another oblation in the Āhavanīya fire. (The leading forth of Agni and Soma)
KB_9.6.5: One should recite over her [the wife] this very verse: "Upa priyaṃ panipnatam. KB_9.6.6:
This is its *yājyā* verse; "Āhutīvr̥dham" is suitable [for it].
(Soma: The Leading Forth of Agni and Soma)
KB_9.6.7: Then they lead the King [Soma] forth by the eastern door.
KB_9.6.8: While he is being led forth, [the priest recites]: "Him, his King Varuṇa; him, the Aśvins... (Soma:
the leading forth of Agni and Soma).
KB_9.6.9: He recites for the one being led forward the verse appropriate [to the occasion]: "And Viṣṇu, possessing friends, unbars the cow-pen.
KB_9.6.10: For the one who has entered, he recites the verse containing the word "entered": "And you have gone within; may you become Aditi."

KB_9.6.11: "Like a hawk [to its] nest, to the seat prepared by prayer; we invoke you, the lord of the hosts. With verses containing the word *sanna* (seated), he praises the one who is seated, [reciting]: "The Asura, the All-God, propped up the sky" (Soma:
during the leading forward of Agni and Soma). KB_9.6.12:
"Thus praise Varuṇa, the Great One"—with this verse containing a benediction (*āśīrvatī*), he performs the concluding rite (*paridhāna*).
He recites verses that are appropriate;
for whatever is appropriate in the sacrifice is successful, and this is for the success of the sacrifice itself.
He recites those twenty verses. They result in the Virāj metre.
KB_9.6.17: Soma is the Virāj.
KB_9.6.18: Food is the Virāj; food is Soma. (Soma: the leading forth of Agni and Soma)
KB_9.6.19: By means of food, he causes that which eats food to prosper.
KB_9.6.20: With the first verse three times and the last verse three times, they amount to twenty-four.
(Soma: The Leading Forth of Agni and Soma)
There are indeed twenty-four half-months in a year;
[this is] for the attainment of the year itself.
(Soma: The Leading Forth of Agni and Soma)
KB_9.6.23: Thus, if they should lead the King [Soma] through the eastern door;
or, indeed, if through the western door.
(The leading forth of Agni and Soma)
KB_9.6.25: The Hotṛ priest should follow along with that very [Soma].
KB_9.6.26: The Hotṛ is indeed the self of the sacrifice.
KB_9.6.27: Soma is the vital breath.
(Soma: The Leading Forth of Agni and Soma) KB_9.6.28:
"Lest I should withdraw my self from this vital breath.
KB_9.6.29: Standing to the north of the south [fire], he performs the enclosing.
Soma the King is indeed glory and food to be eaten. From that [world] above, he thus bestows glory upon himself from this side; he bestows glory.
(The leading forth of Agni and Soma)

KB_10.1.1: This sacrificial post (yūpa) is indeed a thunderbolt (vajra). KB_10.1.2: Therefore, when they erect the sacrificial post on the day of preparation (upavasatha), KB_10.1.3: they strike away the evil from the sacrificer by means of that very thunderbolt.
(On the Animal Sacrifice: An Inquiry into the Sacrificial Post) KB_10.1.4:
It should not be as if it were bent away. KB_10.1.5:
For this is the form of one who is hungry.
KB_10.1.6: [The sacrificial animal] appears as if bent down by its belly.
(The Examination of the Sacrificial Post) KB_10.1.7: Then, having turned back again toward the Āhavanīya fire—
That, indeed, is the form of one who is well-fed. Those wives of his become subject to hunger who construct a sacrificial post (*yūpa*) of such a form. (The Sacrificial Post:
An Investigation into the Sacrificial Post)
One who desires Vedic splendor (*brahmavarcasa*) should make [the sacrificial post] of *pālāśa* wood; one who desires food (*annādya*) should make it of *bailva* wood;
one who desires heaven (*svarga*) should make it of *khadira* wood.
It should be three *aratnis* in measure, corresponding to the form of the worlds; it should be four *aratnis* in measure, corresponding to the form of the animals.
KB_10.1.15: Five cubits long, in the form of the Paṅkti meter.
KB_10.1.16: Six cubits long, in the form of the seasons. KB_10.1.17: Seven cubits long, in the form of the meters.
(The Sacrificial Post: An Inquiry into the Post) KB_10.1.18: Eight cubits long, it is the form of the Gāyatrī. KB_10.1.19: Nine cubits long, it is the form of the Bṛhatī.
Ten *aratni*s in measure, by the form of the *virāj*; eleven *aratni*s, by the form of the *triṣṭubh*.
(The Sacrificial Post: An Investigation of the Post)
KB_10.1.22: It is twelve *aratnis* in length, corresponding to the form of the *jagatī* [meter].
(The Sacrificial Post: An Investigation of the Post) KB_10.2.1:
These are the measures and perfections of the sacrificial post.
KB_10.2.2: Having prepared one of these [measures] to perfection, one should make the sacrificial post (*yūpa*).
(The Investigation of the Sacrificial Post regarding Animals) KB_10.2.3: Regarding this, they say: "One must not cut down the sacrificial post."
KB_10.2.4: It should indeed be unlimited. KB_10.2.5: For one certainly conquers the measured with the measured. (The Examination of the Animal Sacrifice and the Post)
KB_10.2.6: [He should offer] the immeasurable with the immeasurable;
KB_10.2.7: for the attainment of the unlimited; KB_10.2.8:
wherever he considers the limit to be in his mind, there he should perform it.
Regarding that, concerning both the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) and the altar (*vedi*), it is said:
"Prajāpati is indeed the mind."
Sacrifice is indeed Prajāpati. (The Contemplation of the Animal and the Post) Sacrifice itself, verily, takes pleasure in the sacrifice.
KB_10.2.13: That which is the mind of the mind;
KB_10.2.14: it is fixed as the sacrificial post (*yūpa*) of the Vājapeya sacrifice, measuring seventeen cubits;
KB_10.2.15: it is established with eight corners.
KB_10.2.16: For the attainment of all desires.
KB_10.2.17: Then he washes it thoroughly.
(Animal sacrifice: consecration of the sacrificial post)
KB_10.2.18: When this [body] becomes as if made cruel by an axe or as if carved by a carpenter; KB_10.2.19: it is this [act] that makes it swell and heals it. KB_10.2.20: Then he anoints it.
(Regarding the consecration of the sacrificial post for the animal sacrifice: Those very waters which are in man, those he thereby places within him.
KB_10.2.23: The sacrificer himself should perform the anointing.
KB_10.2.24: In this way, the sacrificer becomes as if free from harshness.
(The consecration of the sacrificial post for the animal sacrifice)
KB_10.3.1: "They anoint you at the sacrifice, O seeker of the gods"—this verse containing the word *akta* ("anointed") and being appropriate, he recites for the post being anointed.

KB_10.3.2: "Rise up, O Lord of the Forest; being established in front of the kindled fire, once born, he is born again in the auspiciousness of the days. Stand upright for our protection; standing upright, protect us from distress with your banner"—these verses containing the words *ucchrayasva* ("rise up") and *ūrdhva* ("upright"), he recites for the post being erected.
(The animal sacrifice: the consecration of the sacrificial post).
KB_10.3.3: With the verse containing the word *parivīta* ("encircled"), "The youth, well-clothed, has come encircled," he performs the act of encircling [the sacrificial post]. KB_10.3.4:
He recites verses that are appropriate [to the occasion].
(Animal sacrifice: preparation of the sacrificial post)
KB_10.3.5: That which is appropriate in the sacrifice is successful; it is for the very success of the sacrifice.
KB_10.3.6: He recites those seven [verses]. (The preparation of the sacrificial post for the animal sacrifice)
There are indeed seven meters; for the attainment of all the meters, he recites the first verse three times and the last verse three times, which results in eleven.
The *triṣṭubh* consists of eleven syllables;
cattle are connected with the *triṣṭubh*. [This is] for the attainment of cattle.
KB_10.3.12: Thus, likewise, in the case of a single sacrificial post and a single animal.
(The consecration of the sacrificial post for the animal).
KB_10.3.13: Now, if they were to immolate the set of eleven animals at a single sacrificial post.
KB_10.3.14: At each and every animal sacrifice, the Adhvaryu gives the command.
KB_10.3.15: At each and every animal sacrifice, the verse "The youth, well-clothed and girt with the cord, has come" is the same concluding verse (*paridhānīyā*) for the one being girt with the cord.
(Regarding the consecration of the sacrificial post for the animal sacrifice) KB_10.3.16: Thus [it is] for a single sacrificial post.
KB_10.3.17: Now, how is it in the case of the eleven sacrificial posts?
KB_10.3.18: One should recite these same seven [verses] over the seventeen [pieces].
(Animal sacrifice: preparation of the sacrificial post) KB_10.3.19: Now, they join together that which is the uppermost.
KB_10.3.20: Whatever remains of that hymn, one should continue reciting it.
(Animal sacrifice: consecration of the sacrificial post) KB_10.3.21:
That [recitation] occurs after the *pragātha*.
KB_10.3.22: "Like the horns of horned animals, they have come together"—this [verse] addresses all [the stakes].
(The preparation of the sacrificial post for the animal sacrifice) KB_10.3.23:
"A youth, well-attired, has come, girt about"—this indeed is the concluding verse; it belongs to the one being girt about.
(Regarding the consecration of the sacrificial post for the animal victim) KB_10.4.1:
Regarding this, they say: "One should throw it [the post] into the fire. KB_10.4.2: For the sacrificial post is indeed the sacrificer.
The Āhavanīya fire is the heavenly world; it is that very fire which leads him to the heavenly world.
(The consecration of the sacrificial post for the animal sacrifice) KB_10.4.4: It is precisely this which leads him to the heavenly world.
KB_10.4.5: "That leads to heaven.
KB_10.4.6: Regarding this, they say: "He should indeed remain standing" [during the consecration of the sacrificial post].
KB_10.4.7: "This place where the *svaru* stands is powerful; may the Asuras and Rākṣasas not descend upon it.
(The animal sacrifice: the preparation of the sacrificial post. KB_10.4.8:
"Therefore, this *vajra* should stand raised upon the sacrificial ground, striking away and driving off the Asuras and Rākṣasas, while guarding both the sacrifice and the sacrificer."
(Regarding the animal sacrifice: the consecration of the sacrificial post) KB_10.4.9:
Now, that which is suitable for the post is of one kind, while that which is for the pit is of another. KB_10.4.10:
That which has its bark facing downwards is for the pit.
One should not go toward its shadow. Now, that sacrificial post which has upward-pointing bark is for human use.
(Regarding the consecration of the sacrificial post for an animal sacrifice:
KB_10.4.13: One may perform that [consecration] at will.
KB_10.4.14: Now, in the case of one whose bark-fibers turn in the counter-clockwise direction following the sun's revolution—
That which is fit for the sacrificial post (*yūpya*) is conducive to heaven; it is singular and excludes rivals. Or rather, that which is covered with *palāśa* leaves from the root upward is so.
KB_10.4.17: That [post] is not naked; it is conducive to cattle.
KB_10.4.18: One who desires cattle should perform that [rite]. (The consecration of the sacrificial post)
KB_10.5.1: He who undergoes initiation enters the mouth of Agni and Soma.
KB_10.5.2: Therefore, on the day of preparation (upavasatha), he immolates the animal dedicated to Agni and Soma.
(Regarding the animal: a discussion on the consumption of its remains)

KB_10.5.3: For this [sacrifice] is indeed the redemption of his own self by means of that which is devoid of action; having redeemed his self and become free from debt, he then performs the sacrifice.
(On the consideration of the consumption of the sacrificial remains) KB_10.5.4: Therefore, one should not eat of it.
KB_10.5.5: For that man is indeed [redeemed] by means of a counterpart.
(The discussion on the consumption of the sacrificial remains for animals) KB_10.5.6: Regarding this, they say: "The oblation, indeed, is the ransom for the self."
KB_10.5.7: At that time, he should not eat even of the sacrificial oblation itself.
(Regarding the consideration of the consumption of the remnants of the animal sacrifice: KB_10.5.8: He should not eat [the remnant] thinking, "This is the ransom for my self."
Therefore, one should eat only when there is desire.
(The discussion on the consumption of the remnants of the animal sacrifice) Agni and Soma are indeed day and night.
KB_10.5.11: In that they proceed with the omentum during the day, by that the day becomes gratified as belonging to Agni. (Paśu: Consideration regarding the consumption of the remains)
It concludes with the night.
By this, the night belonging to Soma is gratified.
This is the liberation from day and night.

KB_10.5.16: By means of the sacrifice lasting more than a day and night, one is released [from the debt to the Pitṛs]. (Paśu: Consideration regarding the consumption of the remnants) KB_10.5.17: Those two do not reach him.
KB_10.5.18: He who, knowing thus, sacrifices this animal—KB_10.6.1:
Regarding it, they say: "It should be of two forms, white and black, according to the forms of day and night."
KB_10.6.2: "Or white and red are the forms of Agni and Soma.

(Regarding the animal sacrifice: the fore-offerings and after-offerings for the animal). KB_10.6.3: For that [sacrifice], there are eleven fore-offerings (*prayāja*), eleven after-offerings (*anuyāja*), and eleven subsidiary offerings (*upayāja*).
(Regarding the animal sacrifice: the fore-offerings and after-offerings for the animal victim) KB_10.6.4: These amount to thirty-three.
KB_10.6.5: Indeed, all the gods are thirty-three.

KB_10.6.6: [The fore- and after-offerings] are for the gratification of all the gods. (Regarding the animal sacrifice: the fore-offerings and after-offerings in the animal sacrifice. KB_10.6.7: The fore-offerings are indeed the out-breaths; the after-offerings are the in-breaths.
Therefore, they are equal;
for these vital breaths, the prāṇa and apāna, are indeed equal.
(The animal sacrifice: the fore-offerings and after-offerings).
Regarding this, they ask: "Why does one sacrifice with a *ṛc* verse at the *prayāja* offerings, but with *pratīkas* (initial phrases) at the *anuyāja* offerings?
The *prayāja* offerings are indeed the emission of semen.
(In the animal sacrifice, there are *prayāja* and *anuyāja* offerings.)
KB_10.6.12: The after-offerings (anuyājas) are the depositing of semen.

KB_10.6.13: Therefore, one sacrifices in the fore-offerings (prayājas) with a Ṛg-verse, and in the after-offerings with the introductory phrases (pratīkas). (Regarding the animal sacrifice: the fore-offerings and after-offerings in the animal sacrifice.)
Now, as for that which he says entirely at the end:
he thereby places the sacrificer in the heavenly world.
(Regarding the animal sacrifice: the fore-offerings and after-offerings).
KB_10.6.16: He gratifies [the deities] with the *āprī* verses.
KB_10.6.17: Indeed, he who sacrifices prepares the sacrifice with his whole self and his whole mind.
(Regarding the animal sacrifice: the *prayāja*s and *anuyāja*s in the animal offering.)
KB_10.6.18: His self becomes, as it were, emptied.
KB_10.6.19: He replenishes him with these *āprī* verses.
(The fore-sacrifices and after-sacrifices in the animal sacrifice.)
Because he propitiates them with that,
they are called *āprīs*.
(The *prayājas* and *anuyājas* in the animal sacrifice.)
KB_10.7.1: He carries fire around the victim for the sake of driving away the Rakṣases.
KB_10.7.2: Agni, indeed, is the driver away of the Rakṣases.
(The carrying of fire around the victim)
He carries the fire around [the victim] three times while it is being procreated. This is just as if one were to construct three fire-walls; such is this act.
(The carrying of fire around the animal)
Therefore, he should say to the fire-kindler, "Go around it again," if he desires that [the victim] should not stray away. (The rite of carrying fire around the animal).

KB_10.7.7: "O divine immolators and you humans, take hold! Bring forward the sacrificial doors, desiring the sacrifice for the two lords of the sacrifice! (This is the *adhrigu* injunction regarding the animal.
KB_10.7.8: Regarding this, some say:
"The sacrificer is indeed the lord of the sacrifice" (KB 10.7.9).
"Who is a human? one should say (KB 10.7.10).
(The *adhrigu* call regarding the animal victim.)
KB_10.7.11: "The deity indeed is the lord of the sacrifice.
KB_10.7.12: "Twenty-six are its ribs. KB_10.7.13: "For the ribs are indeed the [sacrificial] portions."
KB_10.7.14: "On both sides [of the animal] there is blood all around"—this is the *adhrigu* call for the victim.
KB_10.7.15: For the *rakṣas* are indeed the vessels of blood.
KB_10.7.16: "Lest I should produce a portion for the gods with a portion belonging to the *rakṣas*," [he says].
(The *adhrigu-praiṣa* regarding the animal sacrifice) KB_10.7.17: This very *adhrigu* is indeed a command.
KB_10.7.18: “Do not cut off the limbs.
KB_10.7.19: “For that which is not defective is the oblation for the gods.
(The Adhrigu-praiṣa regarding the animal sacrifice)
KB_10.7.20: "Truly, they do not eat the defiled oblation.
KB_10.7.21: "Nine times [he says] 'O Adhrigu, blow! KB_10.7.22: "These vital breaths are nine."
(Adhrigu-praiṣa for the animal sacrifice) KB_10.7.23:
He thereby places the vital breaths within the sacrificer; KB_10.7.24: for the sake of full longevity in this world.
(Adhrigu-praiṣa for the sacrificial animal):
"For immortality, in that world.
He performs the three-fold enclosure so that it may not be turned back.
KB_10.7.27: He recites once at the beginning.
(The *adhrigu* call for the animal sacrifice) KB_10.7.28:
For the ancestors are, as it were, only once.
KB_10.7.29: Indeed, the animal being immolated becomes as if dedicated to the ancestors and the deities.
(The *adhrigu* formula for the animal sacrifice) KB_10.7.30: Now, as to why he recites it three times subsequently.
They indeed have three deities;
thus he makes it belong to the gods, free from any lapse.
(The *adhrigu* call regarding the animal sacrifice)
KB_10.8.1: Having put on [the garment], he mutters in a low voice: "Both are sinless...
KB_10.8.2: For the slaughterer (*śamitṛ*) of the gods is indeed sinless.
(The *adhrigu* injunction regarding the animal sacrifice)
For this very reason, he hands him over to that [Agni];
for he indeed knows the gods.
(The Adhrigu-praiṣa regarding the sacrificial animal)
Then he recites the *stokīyā* verses.
By means of these, he makes the drops (*stokas*) palatable for Agni.
Indeed, these are their *puronuvākyās*, and these are their *yājyās*.
Therefore, they become handsome. (Paśu: Stokānuvacana) KB_10.8.8: Therefore, they become handsome. (Paśu: Stokānuvacana)
KB_10.8.9: Having performed [the rites] with the *svāhā*-utterances, they proceed with the omentum (*vapā*).
KB_10.8.10: By doing so, they make the *prayāja* offerings share in the animal sacrifice.
KB_10.8.11: One should not release speech between the *svāhā*-utterances and the omentum.
The *svāhā*-utterances are indeed the vital breaths;
the omentum is the self.
KB_10.8.14: "He does not separate these vital breaths and the self from one another.

(The omentum sacrifice of the animal victim) KB_10.8.15: Now, as for the fact that the *anuṣṭubh* verses serve as the invitatory prayers (*puronuvākyā*) for the animal victim dedicated to Agni and Soma.
KB_10.8.16: That which is the *anuṣṭubh* is indeed the *gāyatrī*. (The animal sacrifice: the offering of the omentum. KB_10.8.17: The *gāyatrī* is the metre of Agni.
Now, as for the fact that the *yājyā* verses are in the *triṣṭubh* meter:
the *triṣṭubh* is the meter of the ruling power (*kṣatra*),
and Soma is the ruling power.
KB_10.8.21: Thus, according to the meters, he gratifies the deities.
(The animal sacrifice: the offering of the omentum) KB_10.8.22: Now, indeed, while the animal is being immolated, the sacrificial cake is subsequently prepared.
Now, where the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*) is offered— that is,
the *paśupuroḍāśa*—
there the *puroḍāśasviṣṭakṛt* offering is immovable (*acyuta*).
Agni is indeed the Sviṣṭakṛt;
therefore, he becomes unshakable.
(The animal sacrifice: the sacrificial cake for the animal).
KB_10.8.26: The Vaiśvāmitra offering of the *puroḍāśa* for the *sviṣṭakṛt* is unshakable.
KB_10.8.29: Having recited the *puronuvākyā*, he sacrifices with a verse belonging to Viśvāmitra.
KB_10.8.30: The *puroḍāśa* is indeed the expansion of the sacrifice.
Viśvāmitra is indeed speech;
by means of speech the sacrifice is performed.
(Paśu: Paśu-puroḍāśa) KB 10.9.1:
Then he recites the Manotā hymn.
KB 10.9.2: For indeed, all the deities approach the animal as it is being immolated, thinking, "He will mention my name; he will mention my name."
In the animal sacrifice, the minds of all those [goddesses] are woven into the animal itself;
he gratifies them here.

KB_20.3.21: "To Viśvadeva, the lord of the good" is the *anucara* for the one who has performed the wedding; its Brāhmaṇa explanation has been stated. (Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_20.3.22: There are two introductory verses (*pratipad*) for the Vaiśvadeva [parvan].
KB_20.3.23: There are two attendants.
(Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha). KB_20.3.24: There are two days and nights.
The year consists of six seasons and is sixfold. Following these are the two, heaven and earth; these two are the supports. (Soma: the Abhiplava Sadaha)
KB_20.3.27: This self has six limbs and is sixfold. KB_20.3.28: Following these two, namely prāṇa and apāna. KB_20.3.29: These are the six vital breaths (prāṇas).
KB_20.3.30: They do not conform to the completion of the year. KB_20.3.31: Neither from the consecration of the self, nor from the consecration of the vital breaths.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_20.4.1: "The god Savitṛ has indeed become worthy of praise for us"—this is the Sāvitra [verse]; its Brāhmaṇa explanation has been stated.
KB_20.4.2: "For they two, Heaven and Earth, are beneficial to all"—this is the Dyāvāpṛthivīya [verse]; its Brāhmaṇa explanation has been stated.
KB_20.4.3: "Tatam me apas tad u tāyate punar" is the *udvat* [verse] for the Ārbhava [Śastra]; its Brāhmaṇa has been explained.
KB_20.4.4: "Devān huve bṛhat-śravasaḥ svastaye" is the *udvat* [verse] for the Vaiśvadeva [Śastra]; its Brāhmaṇa has been explained.
KB_20.4.5: “Now, of the vigorous, manly, ruddy [steed]... is the Vaiśvānara hymn; it contains the word *vṛṣan* (bull/vigorous).
KB_20.4.6: For Indra is indeed a bull (*vṛṣan*).
(Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_20.4.7: The Triṣṭubh is the bull;
KB_20.4.8: therefore [the verse] contains the word "bull" (vṛṣan).
(Regarding the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* of the Soma sacrifice:
"To the bull-like host, well-sacrificing, wise"—this is the hymn to the Maruts; it contains the word *vṛṣan* ("bull"), and its *brāhmaṇa* has already been explained.
(Regarding the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* of the Soma sacrifice.)

KB_20.4.10: With the verse, "By sacrifice, prosper Jātavedas," they perform the *jātavedasīya* rite. KB_20.4.11: With the verse, "The well-kindled, rich in nourishment, the sun-like one," they perform the *udvat*; its Brāhmaṇa explanation has already been stated. KB_20.4.12: By means of the second day, they attain the world of the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*).
Vāyu, the god among the deities;
vitality as the over-being, they place breath within themselves. (Soma: the Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)
They undertake the third day of the Āyus [Sāman].
Its metrical forms (*chando-rūpa*) are exactly those which belong to the third day [of the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha].
KB_20.5.3: "O Agni, bring the Vasus here"—with these words [he offers] the clarified butter.
KB_20.5.4: This very metre is self-acquired, in that it is brought into correspondence with the form of the day.
(The Soma sacrifice: the Abhiplava ṣaḍaha).
"O you who have red horses and delight in songs, bring hither those thirty-three," so it is said.
That is the form of the third day.
The *praūga* hymn belongs to Uṣṇih and Viśvamanas.
When the *rathantara* sāman was being created, the *prauga* śastra of Vaiśvamanas Auṣṇiha was created after it. By means of that form, he brings the ritual action to fulfillment.
(The *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*)
KB_20.5.10: Indeed, that ritual act which is rich in form is successful.
KB_20.5.11: "Him, him indeed for great success"—this is the introductory verse (*pratipad*) of the *marutvatīya* litany.
KB_20.5.12: "Him, him" is the melodic descent (*ninarti*).
(The *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* of the Soma sacrifice): The third day is at the end.
Having gone as if to the very end, he dances.
KB_20.5.15: For what indeed could go from there?
KB_20.5.18: "Let Brahmanaspati go forth"—thus the Pravān [verse] belongs to Brahmanaspati. (Soma:
Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)
"Three"—this is the form of the third day.
"Let Brahmanaspati go forth"—the Brāhmaṇaspatya [stotra] begins with this.
(Soma: Abhiplava Sadaha)
KB_20.5.19: "May the divine *sūnṛtā* come forth"—this is the *ninartī*.
KB_20.5.20: It occurs at the end of the third day.
KB_20.5.21: Or rather, having reached the very end, it dances as it were.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_20.5.22: For what reason would one depart from that?
KB_20.5.23: There are three *pratipads* for the Marutvatīya [stotras], three *anucarās*, and three [stotras] for Brāhmaṇaspati.
(Regarding the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* of the Soma sacrifice: There are indeed these three worlds;
it is by means of this that they attain these very worlds.
KB_20.5.26: "tiṣṭhā harī rathā yujyamānā" is the Marutvatīya [śastra]. KB_20.5.27:
It is called "sthitavat" because it contains the word "tiṣṭha" (stand).
That is its internal form;
the third day is within it.
KB_20.5.30: It stands as if having reached the end. (Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_20.5.31: For how could it go from there?
KB_20.5.32: "Now I shall proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra"—this is the *niṣkevalya* [śastra].
(Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_20.5.33:
Its internal characteristic (*antarūpa*) is the same as that of the day devoted to recounting past events: "He slew the serpent; he released the waters."
KB_20.5.34: That which is "as if toward what has come to be" (the *abhiplava* six-day period).
KB_20.6.1: "Upward indeed this god Savitṛ [has shone] with golden [hands]"—this is the *Sāvitra* [verse].
KB_20.6.2: "He sprinkles his hands with ghee, the sacrifice," thus it is ghee-rich.
(Soma: Abhiplava Sadaha) KB_20.6.3: Ghee indeed belongs to many deities.
The third day has many deities; therefore, it contains ghee. (Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_20.6.5: Therefore, it is rich in ghee.

KB_20.6.6: "The heaven and earth are covered with clarified butter"—this is the *dyāvāpṛthivīya* [hymn]; it contains *ghṛta*, and its *brāhmaṇa* has already been explained. (Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_20.6.7:
"They fashioned the well-rolling chariot with skillful work"—this is the *ārbhava* [hymn].
KB_20.6.8: "They fashioned the two bay steeds that carry Indra, the powerful ones, the possessors of wealth"—this is the *ninartih* chant.
(Soma: the Abhiplava Sadaha).
KB_20.6.9: The third day is at the end.

KB_20.6.10: Having gone as far as the end of the *nīvāra* grass, he dances. KB_20.6.11: For how could one go from there [otherwise]? KB_20.6.12: "May auspicious intentions come to us from every side"—this is the verse for the Viśvedevas.
"The protectors, not failing in vigor, day by day..."—this is the *ninarti*.
KB_20.6.14: It occurs on the third day from within.
Having gone as far as the edge of the water, he dances;
for how could he go from there [otherwise]?
KB_20.6.17: "To Vaiśvānara, the prayer, O increasers of Truth"—this is the [verse] for Vaiśvānara.
KB_20.6.18: "Like purified ghee, for Agni, you are the people"—thus it is possessed of *ghṛta*; its Brāhmaṇa explanation has been stated.
(Soma: the Abhiplava Ṣaḍaha)
KB_20.6.19: "O Rudras, accompanied by Indra, being of one accord..."—this is for the Maruts.
KB_20.6.20: "Like springs of water in the thirst-stricken heaven, seeking the waters..."—(this is for Soma: the Abhiplava ṣaḍaha).
"By day"— this is the form of yonder world.
"Thee, O Agni, those seeking the *ṛta* have kindled"— this is the *jātavedasīya* [śastra] for the six-day period of the *abhiplava*.

KB_20.6.23: "Tvām tvām" and so forth; KB_20.6.24: Just as [a rite] has a concluding verse (*udarka*), so too does that which has a beginning (*saprabhṛti*) have an internal form (*antarūpa*). (Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)
By means of the third day, they attain this world;
[they attain] the god Āditya among the deities. (Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)
KB_20.6.27: Form is the over-world (*adhibhūta*); the eye is the self (*ātman*). They bestow [it] upon the eye-self; they bestow [it] upon the eye-self.
(The *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*) KB_21.1.1: The gods, desiring to strike away death and evil, and longing for co-residence (*salokatā*) and union (*sāyujya*) with Brahman, perceived this *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*.
Having traversed by means of this *abhiplava* six-day period, they struck down death and evil, and attained co-residence and union with Brahman.
(Soma: *Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*)
In the very same way, the sacrificers, having traversed by means of this very *abhiplava* [six-day period], strike away death and evil, and attain co-residence and union with Brahman. (Soma:
the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*) Having traversed by means of this preceding three-day period, they strove on the fourth day with the *gavāmayana* for the sake of going forward alone.
They enter upon the fifth day, the Āpyūḥ, for the sake of attaining full life-span;
they turn back from the sixth day, the Jyotis, on the far side, so as not to follow after death or evil.
KB_21.1.7: On the fourth day they perform the Gāyatrī [chant].
(The six-day Abhiplava period of the Soma sacrifice) KB_21.1.8: Its metrical forms (*chando-rūpa*) are exactly those of the fourth day.
KB_21.1.9: "The Hotṛ has been born, the conscious one"—thus the *ājya* [laud] contains a reference to birth. KB_21.1.10:
Indeed, that which contains a reference to birth is the characteristic form of the fourth day [of the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*].
The *praūga* hymn belongs to Medhātithi.
Indeed, as the *bṛhat* sāman was being created, the *praūga* hymn of Medhātithi was created after it.
(Soma: the six-day *abhiplava* sacrifice)
KB_21.1.13: It accomplishes the ritual action through its form.
KB_21.1.14: Indeed, that ritual action is successful which is perfected in its form.
(The *abhiplava* six-day period).
KB_21.1.15: “Thou hast been born fierce for victorious power” is the Marutvatīya [śastra], containing the word *jāta*.
KB_21.1.16: Indeed, the form of the fourth day contains the word *jāta*. (Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)
KB_21.1.17: "The fierce one, self-dependent, was born for valor"—this is the *niṣkevalya* [śastra] as if it were already born.
(Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_21.1.18: Indeed, the form of the fourth day is that of something already born.
KB_21.2.1: "That great and desirable [gift] of the god Savitṛ"—this is the verse addressed to Savitṛ.
KB_21.2.2: "Savitṛ has generated the well-pleasing, praiseworthy [offspring]"—this is the verse concerning birth.
KB_21.2.3: Indeed, the form of the fourth day consists of [verses] containing the word "born" (*jāta*). (Soma: the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*) KB_21.2.4:
For the hymn to Heaven and Earth begins with, "O Heaven and Earth, you who are beneficial to all. (*dyāvāpṛthivīyam*)
KB_21.2.5: "The two well-born Dhishaṇās have come between," [this is] like something born. KB_21.2.6: Indeed, the form of the fourth day is like something born.

KB_21.2.7: "Born without a horse, without reins, worthy of praise"—thus the *ārbhava* [laud] contains the word "born" (*jāta*). (Soma: the six-day *abhiplava*) KB_21.2.8: Indeed, the form of the fourth day consists of the word "born."
KB_21.2.9: "Agni, Indra, Varuṇa, Mitra, Aryaman"—this is for the Viśvedevas. KB_21.2.10:
"Having generated the sacrifice, they have fashioned it for me"—this is [the verse] containing the word "born" (*jātavat*).

KB_21.2.11: Indeed, the form of the fourth day consists of [verses] containing the word *jāta*. (Regarding the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*: KB_21.2.12: The hymn to Vaiśvānara begins with "To Vaiśvānara of broad radiance, O sage. It is the *vaiśvānarīya* [hymn].
KB_21.2.13: "In him the sacrificer has gathered blessings," as it were.
(Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_21.2.14: Indeed, the form of the introductory rite (*prāyaṇīya*) is that of the fourth day.
(Regarding the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*): The fourth day is indeed the *punar-prāyaṇīya*.
[The verse] "The world-filling one, the two worlds" (*jātāpṛṇo bhuvanāni rodasī*) contains the word "born" (*jāta*).
KB_21.2.17: The form of the fourth day indeed contains the word *jāta*.
KB_21.2.18: The hymn to the Maruts, beginning with *pra ye śumbhante janayo na saptayaḥ*, contains the word *jāta*.
The form of the fourth day indeed consists of [verses] containing the word *jāta*.
"The guardian of the people, the watchful one, has been born"— this verse addressed to Jātavedas contains the word *jāta*.
The form of the fourth day is indeed that which contains the word "born" (*jāta*).
By means of the fourth day, they obtain food.
The god Candramas among the deities;
the quarters as the over-being; they place the sense of hearing in the self.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_21.3.1: They enter upon the fifth day, which has life as its fifth element.
KB_21.3.2: Its metrical forms (*chando-rūpa*) are the very same as those of the fifth day.

KB_21.3.3: "O Agni, bring the most powerful [strength]"—this is the *ājya* [verse]. (Soma: the six-day *abhiplava*) KB_21.3.4: "May he [lead] us with abundant wealth"—thus, by the word "wealth" (*rāyā*), it refers to that which possesses wealth (*rayimat*).
"Rayimad" (possessing wealth), so it is said, is its form.
That which possesses "adhyāsa" (superimposition) is the form of the *paṅkti* [metre].
The *praūga* is to be taken together.
Indeed, when the *rathantara* sāman was being created, the *praūga* was created following it.
(Soma: the six-day *abhiplava*).
KB_21.3.9: By means of that form, one brings the ritual action to fulfillment.
KB_21.3.10: Indeed, that ritual action which is perfected in its form is truly capable of fulfillment.
(The Soma sacrifice: the Abhiplava ṣaḍaha)

KB_21.3.11: "Where is his hero? Who has seen Indra?"—this is the *marutvatīya* [śastra]. KB_21.3.12: "He who, armed with the thunderbolt, seeking wealth, desires the pressed Soma"—[the word] "wealth" (*rayā*) means "possessing wealth" (*rayimat*).
(The *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* [Soma sacrifice])
KB_21.3.13: "Possessing wealth" is indeed its form.
KB_21.3.14: At the *etā* [chant], the *niṣkevalya* [laud] begins with "Come hither, O Indra, with the cattle. (This refers to the six-day *abhiplava* period.)
"Seeking cattle" means rich in livestock;
"rich in livestock" is indeed its form.
"Up has risen this god Savitṛ with his golden [hands]" is the verse dedicated to Savitṛ.
KB_21.3.18: “He sprinkles his hands with ghee, O Makha”—by saying “with ghee,” it is [a sign] of abundance in cattle.
KB_21.3.19: Indeed, its form is that which possesses cattle.
(Regarding the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* of the Soma sacrifice:

"The two [worlds] rich in ghee, the glory of all beings"—this is the verse addressed to Heaven and Earth (*dyāvāpṛthivīya*). Its Brāhmaṇa explanation has already been stated regarding the [verse] containing the word "ghee.
(Regarding the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* of the Soma sacrifice.)
KB_21.3.21: “The waters have spread out for me; they are spread out again”—this is the Ārbhava [Śastra].
KB_21.3.22: “With knowledge, let us offer with the ladle as if with clarified butter”—it is said that its Brāhmaṇa explanation concerns the offering of *ghṛta* (clarified butter).
(Soma: the Abhiplava Ṣaḍaha)

KB_21.3.23: "In whose course is the speech of the gods?"—this is for the Viśvedevas. KB_21.3.24: "A winner of a thousand, as if in the winning of the sacrifice, by himself"—the phrase "winner of a thousand" refers to the possession of cattle.
(Soma: the Abhiplava Sadaha)
KB_21.3.25: "Possessing cattle" (paśumat) is indeed its form.
KB_21.3.26: "Now, of the nourishing, virile, ruddy one... (pṛkṣasya vṛṣṇo aruṣasya nū saha) is the verse addressed to Vaiśvānara.
KB_21.3.27: "...the buffaloes seized [him] in the lap of the waters" (apām upasthe mahiṣā agṛbhṇata); by the word "buffaloes" (mahiṣāḥ), it is "possessing cattle."
(Regarding the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* of the Soma sacrifice:
Its form is indeed "possessing cattle" (*paśumat*).
The hymn to the Maruts begins with: "Forward for the sake of prosperity, O you who overcome the enemy, you who bestow gifts. (*pravaḥ spaḍ akran suvitāya dāvane*) KB_21.3.29.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) (Spaḍakrant???
KB_21.3.30: "Like the preeminent horn of cattle for the sake of beauty"—the phrase "like the cattle" indicates possession of livestock.
KB_21.3.31: Or its form is "possessing cattle" (*paśumat*).
KB_21.3.32: "O bright one, the growth of the young infant"—this is the *jātavedasīya* verse.
KB_21.3.33: "To the most powerful, the victorious, the well-favored"—[here] "vājinn" means "possessing cattle."
"Rich in cattle," indeed, is its form;
"possessing a superimposition" is the form of the *paṅkti* [verse].
By means of the fifth day, they obtain cattle;
[they obtain] Rudra, the god among the deities.
They bestow glory as the overlord and vigor upon the self.
(The *abhiplava* six-day period: They enter the sixth day as light.
KB_21.4.2: Its metrical forms are the same as those of the sixth day.
KB_21.4.3: "O friends, [bring] together your [offerings] in harmony"—this is the *ājya* [stotra]. (Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha)
"Friends"—this is a form that encompasses all forms.
Indeed, the sixth day is of all forms;
therefore, he addresses everyone with the word "friends."
The *prauga* is to be gathered together. Indeed,
when the *bṛhat* sāman was being created, the *prauga* that is to be gathered together was created after it.
By means of that form, he brings the rite to fulfillment; for indeed,
a rite that is perfect in its form is one that is destined to succeed.
KB_21.4.11: “Great is Indra, manly, filling the people”—this is the *marutvatīya* [śastra]. KB_21.4.12:
“Broad, wide, well-made by the makers”—this is the *ninarta*.
(Regarding the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* of the Soma sacrifice: KB_21.4.13: [The ritual] ends with the sixth day.
KB_21.4.14: Having reached the end as it were, he dances.
KB_21.4.15: For what reason would one go from there?
(The *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* [six-day period] of Soma).
KB_21.4.16: "He who, as soon as born, was the first possessed of mind"—this is the *niṣkevalya* [śastra].
KB_21.4.17: Its internal form is precisely that which restates what has come to be, namely: "He who made the dark-colored one, the lower one, into a cave.
(The Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_21.4.18: That which is here as if it were already existent.
KB_21.4.19: It includes the *udarka*; that is the second internal form.
(The *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*) KB_21.5.1: "That great desirable boon of the god Savitṛ"—this is the *sāvitra* [verse].
KB_21.5.2: "The upholder of heaven, Prajāpati of the world.
KB_21.5.3: "Of heaven"—this is the form of yonder world.
KB_21.5.4: "Heaven and earth are covered with ghee"—thus, the verse addressed to Heaven and Earth contains the word *ghṛta*.
Clarified butter belongs to all the deities;
the sixth day belongs to all the deities.
KB_21.5.7: Therefore, [the *ṣaḍaha*] is like clarified butter. (The *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*: KB_21.5.8:
"Why has the most excellent one, why has the youngest one not come?"—this is the *ārbhava* [laud].
KB_21.5.9: "The most excellent, the youngest"—this is the *ninarti* chant.
KB_21.5.10: The sixth day is internal [to the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*]. (Soma: the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*)

KB_21.5.11: Having gone to the end of the *nīvāra* grains, he dances. KB_21.5.12: For how could one go from there [otherwise]? KB_21.5.13: "O Agnis accompanied by Indra, you have awakened"—this is the verse for the Vaiśvadeva offering.
Its internal form is that which has a concluding verse (*sodarka*).
KB_21.5.15: "To Vaiśvānara, the prayer, O increasers of Truth"—this is the hymn addressed to Vaiśvānara.

KB_21.5.16: "Like clarified butter purified for Agni, you are born for the people"—thus the Brāhmaṇa regarding that [verse] has been stated as being characterized by *ghṛta* (clarified butter). (Soma:
the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_21.5.17: "The Maruts, who pour forth streams, possess bold vigor"—this is the hymn to the Maruts.
KB_21.5.18: "The showerer" is the name for the *ninarta* dance.
KB_21.5.19: It occurs within the sixth day.
KB_21.5.20: Or rather, having gone to the end, he dances as if descending.
KB_21.5.21: For one should go from there to Kardya.
(The Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha of Soma) KB_21.5.22:
"O Agni, you with your days; you, the one desiring to shine"—this is the Jātavedasīya [stotra].
KB_21.5.23: It begins with "tvam tvam" (you, you). KB_21.5.24:
Just as [a rite] has a concluding finale (*sodarka*), so too does that which ends with a *prahṛti* have an internal form (*antarūpa*).
KB_21.5.25: By means of the sixth day, they obtain the waters. (The *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* [six-day period] of the Soma sacrifice) KB_21.5.26: [They obtain] Prajāpati, the god among the deities.
KB_21.5.27: They place the immortal light as the overlord within the self.
(The *abhiplava* six-day period of the Soma sacrifice) KB_21.6.1:
Regarding this they say: "Why does he recite only the *vaiśvadeva* hymns at the end, and not those addressed to a single deity or two deities?"
KB_21.6.2: It does not become exhausted by an offering to a single deity;
KB_21.6.3: nor by one to two deities.
(Regarding the *abhiplava-ṣaḍaha* of the Soma sacrifice:
By means of the Vaiśvadeva [offering], that which has already been traversed becomes [renewed].
Therefore, one should perform the Vaiśvadeva offerings at the end.
For the sake of the strength of these very days;
for the sake of the non-equal vigor of these *abhiplava* periods.
(Soma: the Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_21.6.8: They enter upon the first day as the Jyotis;
KB_21.6.9: by means of the very form of that one-day sacrifice.
(Soma: Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha) KB_21.6.10: For this [Ekāha] is the light of the subsequent days.
KB_21.6.11: The Gāyatra [Sāman] is the second.
KB_21.6.12: For by means of this [six-day period], they go forth.
(The *Soma* sacrifice: the *Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha*) KB_21.6.13: The third [part] is the life-span (*āyus*).
KB_21.6.14: For by means of this [Abhiplava-ṣaḍaha], they go forward.
KB_21.6.15: The first and the last days are Agniṣṭomas.

*svarasāman*)
"However, the *pṛṣṭha* stotras should consist of the *svaras*, so said Kauṣītaki;
for these are indeed *svarasāmans*."
By means of the *pṛṣṭha* chants, the gods indeed touched the heavenly world. Therefore, when the *pṛṣṭha* chants are performed with the *svaras*,
it is for the sake of touching the heavenly world.
(Soma: Svarasāman) KB_24.8.1:
Of the compressed *pṛṣṭhya-ṣaḍaha*, those which are the introductory verses (*pratipad*) of the *vaiśvadeva* [śastra] of the first three-day period (*tryaha*) are the introductory verses.
KB_24.8.2: Those which are the third pressings (*tṛtīyasavana*) of the second three-day period are the third pressings, together with their following [ritual elements].
In that regard, having extracted those *vaiśvadeva* [verses] from there, other, different, unexpressed (*anirukta*) verses addressed to Prajāpati, which are implicitly *vaiśvadeva*, are inserted.
(Soma: Svarasāman)
"O you of swift wrath, [I offer] to you the flowing drop, the draught; as of old, as formerly, as always, as now—where indeed is such a vessel for men who seek the gods?
(Soma: Svarasāman) (Viśvathemathā?)
KB_24.8.5: [The hymn] *prati nābhānediṣṭhaḥ*. KB_24.8.6:
Indeed, those [verses] which explicitly mention the Viśvedevas should be recited as the limits.

Prajāpati is the Svarasāmans.
They conclude as either Agniṣṭomas or Ukthyas;
according to the Paiṅgya tradition, they are Agniṣṭomas.
Those who perform Agniṣṭomas become possessed of the splendor of sacred knowledge (*brahmavarcasa*). "They should be Ukthya sacrifices," so said Kauṣītaki.
That sacrificial rite (*yajña-kratu*) is indeed successful which is an *ukthya*;
for it has fifteen stotras.
The *soma* sacrifices have fifteen recitations (*śastra*).
These amount to thirty chant-recitation pairs (*stotra-śastra*).
He attains the Virāj;
the Virāj is prosperity, the eating of food.
For the attainment of glory, of the Virāj, and of food; for the attainment of glory, of the Virāj, and of food.

from that, this Āditya was born in the sixth month.

"sūryavat" (like the sun), "bhānumat" (radiant), "jyotiṣmat" (luminous), "rukmatvat" (shining like gold), and "rucitavat" (splendid).

For from the ocean this [Soma] rises up from the waters.

That is the form of this day.
When these are recited together, they amount to twenty-one *anuṣṭubh* verses.

Then they cause him to prosper in his own form.

[the Viṣuvat].

That is the form of this day.

"The heroes for their bodies, in the winning of the sun"— this is addressed to Sūrya.
That is the form of this day. (Soma:

"Every day, with benevolent minds and clear vision"— this is the established *saṃhita-pāṭha* of the *saurya* [verse].

The morning litany (prātar-anuvāka) is indeed Prajāpati. They should recite it without delay; they should not let it fall into darkness. That is its successful performance.

namely, that all the *pṛṣṭha* [stotras], all the *stomas*, and the high and low [melodies] are brought together.

the Bṛhat is performed during the third Pavamāna stotra;
the Śākvara is for the Maitrāvaruṇa priest.
The Vairūpa belongs to the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin;
the Raivata belongs to the Acchāvāka.
They thus reach this thirteenth additional month.
For this is the thirteenth [day].
They proceed with the *pṛṣṭhya* days.
KB_25.10.18: For this [sacrifice], the *ājya* chant is the Vairāja hymn beginning with "The men kindle Agni with their thoughts from the two fire-sticks" (*tasya agnim naro dīdhitibhir araṇyoḥ*).

The *pṛṣṭha* chant is the Vairāja; its Brāhmaṇa explanation has already been stated.

KB_25.10.28: For that position of the Vairāja is not subject to the insertion of the *nyūṅkha*.
(Regarding the *Viśvajit* [Soma sacrifice]:
"That indeed was the eldest among beings"—this is the *niṣkevalya* [śastra].
Sacrifice, indeed, is the eldest among beings.
The sacrifice is indeed Prajāpati, the Viśvajit.
Now, that which is the third pressing of the sixth day is the [true] third pressing.
The sixth day belongs to Prajāpati;
Prajāpati is the Viśvajit.
KB_25.11.7: The first day is a one-day rite.

The one-day sacrifice (*ekāha*) is indeed a foundation; it is for the sake of stability.

Regarding this, they ask: "Now, why is it that at the third pressing (*tṛtīyasavana*) of the *viśvajit*, the one-day sacrifice with all the *pṛṣṭha*-stotras, the artistic songs (*śilpa*) are recited, whereas at the midday pressing of the *agniṣṭoma* they are not?
(Soma: *viśvajit*)
KB_25.11.11: Or rather, those breaths which are directed downward are the *śilpas* (arts).
KB_25.11.12: Man, indeed, is the sacrifice. KB_25.11.13: Those breaths of his which are upward are the morning pressing (*prātaḥsavana*).
The midday pressing is the self;
those [stotras] which are downward-facing are the third pressing, and they are the artistic crafts.
Therefore, at the third pressing, the artistic songs (*śilpa*) are recited;
for this is their proper abode.
Now, as for the fact that in the Agniṣṭoma, in the sacrificial session lasting a year, in the Viśvajit which includes all the *pṛṣṭha* chants, the artistic songs (*śilpāni*) are recited at midday.
(Soma: Viśvajit)
The *pṛṣṭha* chants are indeed the self (*ātman*);
the *śilpa* chants are the vital breaths (*prāṇa*).
Indeed, the vital breaths are not manifested apart from the self.
KB_25.11.22: There is no self apart from the vital breaths. KB_25.11.23: These two are not separate.
Therefore, even in the Agniṣṭoma, the artistic hymns (*śilpa*) are recited at midday; [the thought being]:
"Lest I should withdraw my self from the vital breaths."
(Soma: Viśvajit) KB_25.12.1: Now, Prajāpati is indeed the Viśvajit;

The sacrifice is fivefold; it is for the attainment of the sacrifice itself.
"Let us not interrupt the artistic performance of the Acchāvāka," they thought.

Indeed, half of the Viśvajit is performed by means of the day.

[It is performed] at midnight.
Indeed, that which is performed elsewhere than at a *sarvavedasa* or a *sattra* is truly a *sarvaparājita*.
Indeed,
that is a total loss of all one's possessions for whoever gives everything away other than at the Viśvajit sacrifice.
If it is the Viśvajit, then it is indeed everything;
and if it is everything, then it is indeed the Viśvajit.
(Soma: Viśvajit)
"Indeed, he who says, 'I do not give everything,' suffers the fate of a *kartaptya* or perishes," so it has been said regarding the *Viśvajit*.
"He wins a thousandfold," so said Kauṣītaki;
for that which is a thousand is indeed everything. (The Viśvajit Soma sacrifice)

for the Vaiśya indeed thrives.

Now, if someone should, through negligence, strike down [the performance] during the *śastra* or the recitation (*anuvacana*), or if there should be doubt—thinking that what was struck down was not perceived and has passed by—one should, while mentally reflecting on the conclusion of the section, turn back, make the struck-down part unstruck-down, and the performance should proceed from the immediate sequence according to the conclusion of the section; thus they deliberate.
(Soma: Chandomas)
Now Paiṅgya used to say: "The performance [of the mantra] should not be immediate; for this mantra which is recited twice because it was not previously stated would be redundant.
Therefore, the performance should not be immediate," so said Paiṅgya. (Soma: Chandomas)
(Kauṣītaki Brāhmaṇa 26.2.3: [Soma: Chandomas]) Now Kauṣītaki used to say: "These rites indeed have limited fruits, in which a limited collection of mantras is employed.
(Soma: Chandomas)
KB_26.2.3: Now, there are those [stotras] with unlimited fruits, in which an unlimited collection of mantras is employed.

(Soma: Chandomas) The unlimited is indeed the mind; Prajāpati is the mind, and Prajāpati is the sacrifice. The sacrifice itself delights in that part of the sacrifice which is the mind. Therefore, because of the continuity of the mind, the performance [of these stotras] should take place immediately [after the Chandomas]. Thus said Kauṣītaki.
"By the measured one, indeed, one conquers the measured; by the unmeasured, the unmeasured; for the sake of attaining the unlimited, this [is performed] without flaw," so said Kauṣītaki.
(Soma: Chandomas)

KB_26.2.3: One should not offer the oblation. Thus, the sacrificer attains all the heavenly worlds, all desires, all prosperities, and all immortality; he surpasses all beings and attains sovereignty, self-rule, and lordship—this is for one for whom this is performed (*soma*:
*chandomāh*). KB_26.2.4:

Now, if after the girding of the sacrificial post, or after the *praṇava* and *vaṣaṭ* calls, or after the *yājyā* and *puronuvākyā* verses, he should become aware [of an omission], Prāgahis used to say: "In this situation, the transgression becomes manifest at that very moment."
"Therefore, at this juncture, a member of the assembly (*sadasya*) should not awaken one who has committed a grave transgression," so Paiṅgya used to say.
(Soma: Chandomas)
"He meets with a pillar, or falls into a pit, or is imprisoned, or perishes," so it is said, "if a member of the assembly points out a gross error that has already occurred.

"There is no returning to what has been done," so Āruṇi used to say; Śvetaketu said, "It is a loss of merit. Therefore, Paiṅgya used to say, "A member of the assembly should not point out a gross error that has already occurred. (Soma: Chandomas)
(Soma: Chandomas) KB_26.2.4:

"That which is omitted or excessive in the sacrifice is indeed a source of distress; the member of the assembly (*sadasya*) should not point it out," so said Paiṅgya. Therefore, one should not have the member of the assembly point out what is omitted or excessive.
(Soma: Chandomas)

Now, it is said that Pratardana Daivodāsi, having approached the sacrificial session (*sattra*) of the Naimiṣīyas, sat down and asked about a doubt: "If a member of the assembly (*sadasya*) were to point out a gross error, or if any one of the officiating priests (*ṛtvij*) were to notice it, how could your rite remain free from flaw?

(referring to the *Chandomas*). They remained silent. Among them was Ālikayu Vācaspati, who was the Brahman priest. He said, "I do not know this. Come, let me ask Jātūkarṇya, the elder teacher of our predecessors."

Regarding the *Chandomas*, Jātūkarṇya used to say: "If one should perform something excessively [ulbaṇa], whether by oneself or if another points it out to him, how can that excess be made non-excessive? One should repeat everything—a restatement, a *nigada*, a *yājyā*, or whatever else—up to the extent of the excess; that is, a verse (*ṛc*), a half-verse, a quarter-verse, a word, or even a single syllable. Thus he said.
(Soma: Chandomas)

Now Kauṣītaki used to say: "One should not repeat a mantra, nor should one offer an oblation; this is 'unblemished' (*anulbaṇa*)," so said Kauṣītaki. For whatever blemish the Hotṛ priests might unknowingly commit in the sacrifice, the divine Hotṛ Agni makes all of that unblemished. This very thing is declared by a Ṛgvedic verse: KB_26.2.5: *atha ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ: na mantraṃ punar brūyāt, nāhutim juhuyāt, anulbaṇam etad iti ha sma āha kauṣītakiḥ. yad dhi hotāro yajñasya kiṃcid ulbaṇam abudhyamānāḥ kurvanti, sarvaṃ tad agnir daivo hotānulbaṇaṃ karoti. tad etad ṛcābhyuditam.*

KB_26.2.6: "When mortals, with simple minds and feeble resolve, do not comprehend the sacrifice, may Agni—the wise Hotṛ who knows the ritual—being the best of sacrificers, worship the gods according to the seasons. And when it is said at the conclusion of the sacrifice: "He has sacrificed (*ayāt*)."

"Jātavedas has sacrificed at this sacrifice"—by saying "Jātavedas has sacrificed at this sacrifice," he says, "having sat down within, as the first among them. When he says, "Agni, the divine Hotṛ, having sat down before the human Hotṛ, shall sacrifice," he thereby says this. With the latter half-verse, or with the preceding *ṛc*, he utters a blessing.
(Soma:
Chandomas) On the sixth day, the gods indeed attained the *stomas* and the months.
Having reached these *stomas*, and being about to combine these very *pṛṣṭhya-stomas* in pairs,
from where indeed would he bring another *stoma*? (The Chandomas)

These two, the *trivṛt* and the *pañcadaśa* *stomas*, carry the seventh day, having become the *caturviṃśa* *stoma*. Then these two, the *saptadaśa* and the *triṇava* *stomas*, carry the ninth day, having become the *aṣṭācatvāriṃśa* *stoma*.
Now, these two stomas—the twenty-onefold and the thirty-threefold—carry the ninth day, having become the forty-eightfold stoma.
(Soma: Chandomas)

they say that these are the seasons.

by means of them, the tenth day is extended.

therefore, the Bṛhat-sāman is performed on each successive day for the sake of strengthening these very days.

Having recited the *bṛhat* expansion, he recites the womb-verse (*yoni*) of the *rathantara*.

for cattle are fourfold.
